Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma

MONDO:0005184 Pathograph 54 Show in embeddings browser pancreatic cancer

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a malignant pancreatic epithelial neoplasm with ductal differentiation. Most tumors harbor an activating KRAS mutation together with alterations in tumor-suppressor pathways, but KRAS-wild-type tumors include distinct actionable drivers. Acinar reprogramming, ductal-origin models and several precursor lesions contribute to current initiation models; ductal morphology does not establish a unique human cell of origin. Desmoplastic fibroblast states, myeloid and lymphoid suppression, altered antigen presentation, nutrient scavenging and metabolic adaptation shape invasion and treatment response. Resectability and metastatic extent determine clinical management. Surgery with systemic therapy offers potential long-term control in selected localized disease; advanced disease is treated with systemic regimens and, in defined molecular subsets, targeted or immune therapies. Daraxonrasib has randomized clinical efficacy in previously treated metastatic PDAC. Its resistance mechanisms now have paired clinical ctDNA evidence, whereas immune-remodeling/checkpoint combinations remain preclinical.

Subtypes

2
Classical Subtype
An expression program enriched for epithelial differentiation. Classical and basal-like states can coexist within a tumor; bulk-expression assignments do not imply immutable, mutually exclusive diseases. The original virtual-microdissection cohorts associated classical tumors with better survival than basal-like tumors.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:26343385 SUPPORT Computational
"we have identified and validated two tumor subtypes, including a 'basal-like' subtype that has worse outcome and is molecularly similar to basal tumors in bladder and breast cancers."
Moffitt et al. used virtual microdissection of gene expression data to identify classical and basal-like subtypes of PDAC, with classical having better prognosis.
Basal-like Subtype
A basal/squamous expression program associated with adverse outcome in the original profiling cohorts. State abundance and plasticity vary within tumors and under treatment. In autochthonous mouse PDAC, basal-state ablation or basal-cell GM-CSF loss disrupted an immunosuppressive circuit and reduced tumors; this is not yet a validated human state-selective treatment.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:26343385 SUPPORT Computational
"patients with basal-like subtype tumors had an overall worse median survival of 11 months and 44% 1-year survival compared to 19 months and 70% 1-year survival for those with classical subtype tumors"
Moffitt et al. demonstrated basal-like subtype has significantly worse survival compared to classical subtype in PDAC.
PMID:42523238 SUPPORT Model Organism
"Knockout of a single cytokine, GM-CSF, specifically in basal cells recapitulated macrophage repolarization and lymphocyte recruitment observed upon basal state ablation and shrank tumors."
Basal-cell-specific genetic perturbation establishes an immune-organizing GM-CSF role in mouse PDAC. Human prognostic association does not establish the same intervention effect.

Mechanistic Hypotheses

2
RAS(ON) Inhibition Remodels the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
ras_on_inhibition_immune_tme_remodeling EMERGING
Evidence balance 2 support
RAS(ON) multiselective inhibition directly remodels PDAC immunity in mouse models, including increased tumor MHC-I, altered myeloid states and T-cell/cDC-dependent responses. Checkpoint cotreatment can deepen control, but optimal partners, Treg behavior and durability vary by model. Neither universal Treg relief nor clinical daraxonrasib-checkpoint benefit is established. Autophagy and FAK are complementary antigen-presentation regulators rather than mutually exclusive alternatives.
Both July OpenScientist reports and their updated assessments remain under kb/hypotheses/Metastatic_Pancreatic_Adenocarcinoma after consolidation into this disease. PMID40057911 was already available when the immune report omitted it; the August 2026 CTLA-4/Treg study is subsequent evidence.

Acquired Resistance to RAS(ON) Multiselective Inhibition
ras_on_inhibitor_acquired_resistance EMERGING
Evidence balance 2 support
Daraxonrasib resistance includes clinical KRAS amplification and other RAS-pathway alterations, with mutant-allele assignment inferred by an exploratory variant-allele-frequency method. Preclinical and limited clinical findings support RTK bypass, MYC-related programs and allele-specific cyclophilin-A or EGFR/wild-type-RAS routes. The 44-patient paired ctDNA study updates the July report: patient mechanisms are no longer wholly unknown, but selected-cohort frequencies, non-genomic routes, pre-existing versus newly selected clones and optimal salvage remain unresolved. Distinct inhibitor classes and combination regimens must be kept explicit.

Discussions and Knowledge Gaps

Which cancer-associated fibroblast programs actively cause T-cell exclusion and checkpoint resistance in PDAC, and which stromal programs are tumor-restraining or merely correlative with desmoplastic burden?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN gap_pdac_caf_program_t_cell_exclusion
Attached to
pathophysiology#Desmoplastic Stroma pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion pathophysiology#Immune Evasion
PDAC desmoplasia is not a single therapeutic target: some CAF states may exclude effector T cells, whereas others may restrain invasion. A patient-derived organ-on-chip experiment can test whether specific CAF programs are causal for immune exclusion and whether reprogramming them improves T-cell cytotoxicity without removing tumor-restraining stroma.

Decision criterion
A causal CAF immune-exclusion program is supported if its induction reduces T-cell entry or killing and its suppression restores checkpoint response. A tumor-restraining CAF state is supported if induction lowers invasion or viability while preserving or improving T-cell function.

Pathophysiology

42
Chronic Pancreatic Inflammation
Inflammation and tissue injury can cooperate with oncogenic KRAS to enable acinar reprogramming and precursor formation. In one adult acinar/centroacinar KRAS-G12V mouse model, chronic pancreatitis was necessary for tumor induction. This is a model-specific requirement, not a claim that every human PDAC requires clinically recognized pancreatitis. Human chronic pancreatitis is a strong risk factor with risk estimates dependent on follow-up and case definition.

PMID:17349585 SUPPORT Model Organism
"These observations suggest that, during adulthood, PDA stems from a combination of genetic (e.g., somatic K-Ras mutations) and nongenetic (e.g., tissue damage) events."
States the two-component model directly: the genetic lesion is modeled by the KRAS node and the nongenetic tissue-damage component is what this node is for.
PMID:35142721 SUPPORT Human Clinical
"There is an increased risk of PDAC in patients with CP, and incidence rates increase with CP disease duration."
The human counterpart of the mouse result, with risk rising as the inflammation persists. PARTIAL because it measures cancer incidence in inflamed pancreata rather than anything at this node itself.
Acinar-to-Ductal Metaplasia
Acinar cells can lose differentiated identity and adopt ductal-like programs during injury and KRAS-driven transformation. ADM is reversible in regenerative settings and is not synonymous with cancer. Persistent oncogenic signaling can channel reprogrammed cells into PanIN. Adult ductal cells can also initiate PDAC with cooperating p53 alterations in mice; the relative contribution of these origins in humans remains unresolved.

KRAS Oncogene Activation
Activating KRAS variants favor persistent RAS-GTP signaling through RAF-MEK-ERK and additional effector networks, supporting proliferation, survival, metabolic rewiring and microenvironmental remodeling. G12D, G12V and G12R are common in PDAC, with allele-specific signaling and inhibitor responses. Most PDACs are KRAS-mutant; KRAS-wild-type cancers require separate driver characterization. KRAS signaling does not itself establish acquisition of a particular tumor-suppressor mutation or therapeutic inhibition.

This review confirms KRAS mutations as the initiating event in PanIN development, with additional tumor suppressor losses driving progression to invasive carcinoma.
Tumor Suppressor Inactivation
Alterations of CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 cooperate with oncogenic signaling. Loss of p16 removes restraint on CDK4/6-RB cell-cycle progression; p53 alterations weaken stress checkpoints and can confer context-dependent gain of function; SMAD4 loss changes TGF-beta responses. Reported alteration frequencies differ with cohort, assay, copy-number detection and inclusion of epigenetic silencing. These are cooperating events rather than consequences inferred from co-occurrence with KRAS.

Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:18772397 SUPPORT Human Clinical
"This list includes the classic tumor suppressor genes CDKN2A (p16), SMAD4, and TP53, as well as genes that had not previously been implicated in pancreatic cancer development."
The landmark Jones et al. genomic analysis identified CDKN2A, SMAD4, and TP53 as core tumor suppressor genes in pancreatic cancer through global sequencing of 24 advanced pancreatic adenocarcinomas.
Pancreatic Precursor Progression and Invasive Growth
KRAS-mutant PanIN can progress with cooperating genetic and microenvironmental changes to invasive, gland-forming PDAC. IPMN and mucinous cystic neoplasms provide additional precursor routes. Not every precursor progresses, and a uniform obligatory mutation order or exclusive acinar origin is not established.
Downstream
Desmoplastic Stroma Tumor-secreted ligands promote fibroblast-state changes and matrix-producing stroma.
Metastatic Dissemination and Colonization Invasive growth enables dissemination, but the timing and route vary across tumors.
IL1-LIF-JAK-STAT Inflammatory Fibroblast Programming The neoplastic epithelial compartment can induce inflammatory fibroblast differentiation through secreted IL1α in PDAC organoid-stellate-cell systems. This branch represents signals from established tumors, not a claim that invasion itself or extracellular matrix deposition directly induces every iCAF state; other ligands contribute in vivo.
Tumor-Restraining Fibroblast Programs Neoplastic cells can establish a Hedgehog-responsive fibroblast-rich stroma with tumor-restraining activity in a genetically engineered PDAC mouse model. This incoming branch concerns the SHH-dependent component of the heterogeneous stromal node, not all fibroblast states or a universal protective role for fibrosis.
Pancreatic Exocrine Functional Loss An established pancreatic tumor can impair exocrine secretion through duct obstruction and loss of functional tissue. Risk depends on tumor location and extent; this is not an obligatory consequence of a noninvasive precursor, and postoperative insufficiency has an additional surgical cause.
Obstructive Jaundice An obstructive pancreatic head cancer can impair bile drainage and cause jaundice. This location-dependent consequence of established tumor growth is not attributed to all PDAC or to noninvasive precursors.

PMID:17349585 SUPPORT Model Organism
"However, if these mice are challenged with a mild form of chronic pancreatitis, they develop the full spectrum of PanINs and invasive PDA."
Genetic and inflammatory cooperation supports progression in the defined mouse model.
PMID:26592447 SUPPORT Model Organism
"In contrast to the lack of response to oncogenic Kras alone, simultaneous activation of Kras and mutant p53 in adult ductal epithelium generated invasive PDAC in 75% of mice as early as 2.5 months after tamoxifen administration."
Cooperating oncogenic KRAS and mutant p53 enable invasive cancer in ductal-origin mice.
Desmoplastic Stroma
Tumor-derived signals and local tissue interactions recruit and alter fibroblast states that deposit collagen, hyaluronan and other extracellular matrix. Dense matrix can impair perfusion, but stromal programs are heterogeneous: some support inflammation or immune exclusion and others restrain tumor growth. Fibroblast depletion and matrix digestion are not interchangeable, and neither is a generally validated treatment for PDAC.

CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion

Some fibroblast and stromal programs constrain PDAC. Immune Evasion
Myeloid suppression, dysfunctional lymphocytes, stromal exclusion and impaired antigen presentation limit immune control in most PDAC. These mechanisms vary between tumors and metastatic sites. Rare mismatch-repair-deficient/MSI-high cancers can respond to checkpoint blockade; PDAC is not uniformly refractory to every immune or targeted therapy.

FAK-Mediated Antigen-Presentation Suppression
Tumor-cell FAK signaling limits immunoproteasome expression and antigen presentation in PDAC models. FAK depletion increases antigen diversity and MHC-I presentation; combined STAT3 loss further promotes immune control. This is a complementary regulator, not evidence that RAS cannot influence MHC-I. The reported antigen-presentation effect is kinase-independent, requires nuclear FAK, and is lost in an extreme squamous phenotype; FAK kinase inhibition is therefore not equivalent to eliminating this function.

Metastatic Dissemination and Colonization
Invasive tumor cells disseminate and establish distant lesions, frequently in the liver and also lung or peritoneum. Colonization depends on both tumor-cell programs and organ-specific niches; metastatic-site immune composition differs from the primary tumor. A single EMT program is not obligatory for every metastatic event.

Perineural Invasion
Pancreatic cancer cells interact with nerves and migrate along neural structures. HGF-MET signaling can activate mTOR-NGF, promoting nerve recruitment and invasion in experimental models. PNI is associated with adverse clinical outcomes and can contribute to pain; it is not established as the universal route to distant metastasis. Human NGF/TrkA levels correlate with PNI and pain in one tissue cohort, but a prospective resectable cohort found pain did not predict PNI; clinical pain and neural invasion are not interchangeable readouts.

Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition
In immunocompetent PDAC models, RAS(ON) multiselective inhibition can reduce suppressive myeloid subsets, increase tumor MHC-I and lymphocyte infiltration, and enable immune-dependent tumor control. RMC-7977 and daraxonrasib provide direct PDAC evidence. Responses and optimal checkpoint partners are model-dependent; increased Tregs and adaptive myeloid rebound can limit benefit. Patient survival from daraxonrasib monotherapy does not establish an immune-mediated clinical benefit.

Acquired RAS(ON) Inhibitor Resistance
Daraxonrasib can initially control PDAC and subsequently lose efficacy through heterogeneous resistance routes. An August 2026 study profiled 44 patients with response or stable disease lasting more than three months followed by progression: 59% had treatment-emergent RAS-pathway genomic alterations, including KRAS amplification in 36%. Mutant-allele identity was inferred from variant-allele-frequency ratios by an exploratory method, not directly confirmed in all cases. These selected-cohort findings establish patient mechanisms but not universal resistance or population-wide route frequencies. Median progression-free survival alone cannot distinguish acquired resistance, primary nonresponse and death. Non-genomic, tissue-specific and low-shedding routes remain incompletely captured.

On-Target RAS Reactivation and KRAS Amplification
Increased mutant KRAS dosage can attenuate daraxonrasib suppression and restore RAS-pathway output in PDAC models. Paired ctDNA detected emergent KRAS amplification in 16/44 profiled PDAC patients after initial disease control. Assignment to the pre-existing mutant allele was inferred from variant-allele-frequency ratios; the supplementary table explicitly calls this exploratory and unconfirmed, rather than direct allele phasing in all cases. Engineered and selected PDAC models provide functional corroboration of mutant KRAS dosage. Secondary KRAS mutations were absent from the 44 PDAC cases and selected PDAC resistance models, while an engineered Ba/F3 deep mutational scan identified resistance-conferring second-site variants in a different context.

Adaptive mTOR and JUN-AP1 Transcriptional Program
CRISPR screens identify mTOR and JUN as convergent mediators of resistance to MAPK-pathway inhibitor combinations. In PDAC cells, JUN overexpression supported resistance to SHP2 plus RMC-6236; in-vivo MAP2K4 rescue used SHP2 plus ERK inhibition. The combination-specific evidence should not be recast as patient-level daraxonrasib monotherapy resistance. A separate RMC-7977 mouse study identified focal Jun gain in one resistant tumor.

MYC Amplification-Driven RAS-Independent Proliferation
RMC-7977-resistant KPC tumors frequently gained Myc copies while maintaining ERK suppression. YAP-TEAD-dependent transcriptional output accompanied resistance, and TEAD cotargeting restored sensitivity in vitro. The subsequent daraxonrasib clinical study detected MYC amplification in one patient together with KRAS amplification and corroborated MYC-related resistance in models. These data support a bypass route without proving that all MYC gain is independent of RAS or that TEAD combinations benefit patients.

USP20 Cholesterol-Metabolism CD8 Exhaustion Checkpoint
KRAS-G12D induces EGR1-USP20, stabilizing HMG-CoA reductase and promoting cholesterol metabolism associated with CD8 exhaustion. KRAS inhibition or cholesterol blockade induces compensatory ULK1-associated autophagy; USP20 also stabilizes ULK1. This is a two-arm metabolic and survival mechanism. MRTX1133 plus USP20 inhibition and PD-1 blockade regressed tumors in preclinical models, but human tissue profiling is not evidence of clinical combination efficacy.

An August 2026 PDAC study found that MRTX1133 or daraxonrasib recruits regulatory as well as effector and exhausted T cells. Basal-State GM-CSF Immunosuppressive Circuit
Basal malignant cells can organize tumor-maintaining fibroblast, macrophage and cytokine states. Lineage tracing found greater plasticity of basal than classical cells in autochthonous mouse PDAC. Basal-state ablation, and separately basal-cell GM-CSF knockout, reprogrammed the stroma and recruited cytotoxic lymphocytes. This establishes a causal circuit in these models while leaving human state-targeting efficacy unresolved.

Pancreatic Exocrine Functional Loss
Tumor-associated obstruction and loss of functional pancreatic tissue can impair digestive enzyme delivery. The resulting maldigestion contributes to nutritional loss; this process also occurs after pancreatic surgery. Clinical prevalence varies with stage, location and testing method.

Adaptive CD24 Antiphagocytic Signaling
In KRAS-G12C-driven mouse PDAC, selective KRAS inhibition upregulated the CD24 antiphagocytic signal despite an inflamed microenvironment. CD24 blockade increased macrophage phagocytosis and sensitized tumors; related findings occurred in G12D PDAC. The preprint and final paper report the same work. This is a plausible immune-adaptation route whose relevance to clinical daraxonrasib progression remains unproven.

Senescent Myofibroblast Immunosuppression
Senescent myofibroblastic CAFs accumulate near tumor ducts and during PDAC progression. Genetic or pharmacologic depletion of senescent stromal cells in mouse models reduced macrophage-associated immune suppression and improved chemotherapy responsiveness. Human tissue identifies the state, but clinical senolytic efficacy is not established.

Infiltrative malignant epithelial glands with ductal differentiation; differentiation can vary and this morphology does not establish an exclusively ductal cell of origin.

Dense collagen-rich fibrotic stroma surrounding malignant glands is a defining histopathologic feature of PDAC.

Daraxonrasib (RAS(ON) Multiselective Inhibitor)
Action: PharmacotherapyNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Pharmacotherapy (NCIT:C15986). NCIT:C15986 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C15986
Agent: daraxonrasib CHEBI:746946 Chemical Entities of Biological Interest (CHEBI) Relation: this treatment uses this therapeutic agent This treatment uses daraxonrasib (CHEBI:746946). CHEBI:746946 is a therapeutic agent from Chemical Entities of Biological Interest.
Daraxonrasib is a cyclophilin-A-dependent inhibitor of active GTP-bound mutant and wild-type RAS. In phase III RASolute 302 for previously treated metastatic PDAC, median overall survival was 13.2 versus 6.6 months in the RAS G12 population (hazard ratio 0.40); median progression-free survival was 7.3 versus 3.5 months. These clinical outcomes establish treatment efficacy, not a universal resistance mechanism or an immune basis for survival benefit.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS KRAS Oncogene Activation — Daraxonrasib directly inhibits the active RAS(ON) state produced by oncogenic KRAS codon-12 mutations, the initiating driver of PDAC, suppressing constitutive RAS-MAPK signaling.
Show evidence (1 reference)

The RASolute 302 report describes daraxonrasib's mechanism as direct inhibition of the active GTP-bound RAS state driven by mutant KRAS in PDAC.
ACTIVATES Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition — Preclinical PDAC immune remodeling follows RAS inhibition; this is not an inferred immune mechanism for the phase III survival effect.

ACTIVATES Regulatory T-Cell Recruitment after KRAS Inhibition — Treg recruitment is a model-dependent adaptation documented with daraxonrasib and MRTX1133.

Pancreatic enzyme replacement, including pancrelipase, is used for exocrine insufficiency and maldigestion when indicated. Diagnosis

3
Pancreatic-Protocol Cross-Sectional Imaging
Multiphasic contrast-enhanced CT establishes lesion anatomy, vascular involvement and metastatic extent. MRI is an alternative or problem-solving examination; resectability requires multidisciplinary interpretation.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:41067164 SUPPORT Other
"Multiphasic contrast-enhanced thoracic-abdominal and pelvic CT, including late arterial phase and portal venous phase, should be used as the first-line imaging modality for suspected pancreatic cancer"
Defines first-line diagnostic imaging.
Tissue Diagnosis
Cytology or biopsy, preferably by endoscopic-ultrasound guidance where appropriate, confirms malignancy before systemic therapy. Tissue morphology and clinical imaging must be reconciled with the differential diagnosis.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:41067164 SUPPORT Other
"Cytology or biopsy proof of pancreatic cancer should be obtained before initiation of ChT in localised disease, preferably by EUS guidance"
Specifies tissue confirmation before chemotherapy.
Germline and Tumor Molecular Testing
Inherited susceptibility testing and tumor profiling identify clinically relevant BRCA, mismatch-repair and other actionable alterations. KRAS-wild-type tumors particularly warrant a search for alternative drivers, including fusions; the result must match the treatment-specific evidence.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:41067164 SUPPORT Other
"BRCA genetic testing should be offered to all patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer"
Supports germline testing in metastatic disease.

Stages

4
Resectable
Localized disease judged technically resectable by multidisciplinary pancreatic-protocol imaging and clinical assessment. Pancreaticoduodenectomy or distal pancreatectomy is selected by location; postoperative systemic therapy is standard for suitable patients.
Borderline Resectable
Localized disease with a high risk of margin-positive resection, commonly related to vascular involvement. Induction therapy and reassessment guide consideration of surgery.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:41067164 SUPPORT Other
"Patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer have a high probability of an R1 resection and should be considered for induction treatment"
Consensus recommendation links borderline resectability to margin risk and induction treatment.
Locally Advanced
Nonmetastatic disease with local involvement precluding upfront resection. Systemic treatment, symptom care and reassessment for selected local approaches are appropriate.
Metastatic
Distant spread, commonly to liver, peritoneum or lung, requires systemic and supportive care. The metastasis, RAS-inhibitor resistance and immune-remodeling mechanisms belong to this PDAC model rather than a separate disease.

"We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial to evaluate the efficacy of olaparib as maintenance therapy in patients who had a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer and disease that had not progressed during first-line platinum-based chemotherapy."
The POLO trial demonstrated that maintenance olaparib significantly prolonged progression-free survival in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer patients who had not progressed on platinum-based chemotherapy.
DOI:10.1200/jco.21.01604 SUPPORT Human Clinical
"No statistically significant OS benefit was observed (median 19.0 v 19.2 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.83; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.22; P = .3487)."
Final POLO analysis qualifies the PFS benefit with the nonsignificant OS comparison.
NCT02715804 PHASE_III
HALO 109-301 compared PEGPH20 plus gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel with placebo plus chemotherapy in hyaluronan-high metastatic PDAC. Increased response rate did not improve survival, limiting clinical translation of stromal hyaluronan depletion.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:32706635 SUPPORT Human Clinical
"The addition of PEGPH20 to AG increased the ORR but did not improve OS or PFS."
Randomized trial limits extrapolation from preclinical matrix/hypoperfusion rescue to clinical survival.
🧫

Experimental Models

1
Human PDAC Cell and Organoid RAS-Response Models ORGANOID
Patient-derived PDAC organoids and established cell models permit driver-specific RMC-7977 sensitivity assays; engineered and selected cell models test bypass mechanisms. These isolated epithelial systems do not reproduce the complete immune or desmoplastic microenvironment.

PMID:38588697

Limitations: Cell viability and target phosphorylation are not patient response or immune-remodeling endpoints.

PMID:38588697 SUPPORT In Vitro
"RMC-7977 exhibited low nanomolar potency on the viability of most human and mouse PDAC cell lines and human PDAC organoids"
Direct cell and organoid assays establish activity with subtype/driver variation, not whole-organism immunity.

2
Immunocompetent Mouse PDAC RAS-Inhibition Models
RMC-7977 and daraxonrasib experiments test tumor regression, immune-cell changes and immunotherapy combinations in immunocompetent PDAC. Results depend on regimen and tumor/host model and do not establish patient immune pharmacodynamics.

"In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment."
Direct PDAC evidence was omitted from the immune report despite being cited in the resistance report.
KPC RMC-7977 Acquired-Resistance Models
Chronic RMC-7977 exposure produces initially responding and subsequently relapsing KPC tumors. MYC and YAP/TEAD programs were interrogated; tool-compound models and clinical daraxonrasib cohorts have different resistance distributions.

Computational Models

2
PDAC CAF-Mediated Invasion PhysiCell Model C++/XML/CSV PhysiCell AGENT_BASED
Grammar-based PhysiCell agent-based model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma neoplastic cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts. The model encodes fibroblast-mediated invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal state switching, and ECM-dependent motility tradeoffs using human-interpretable cell rules informed by PDAC spatial transcriptomics and coculture data.

The pinned v2.0.1 repository, XML configurations and rule tables were inspected in this review. This is a published computational model record; no simulation, calibration or patient-response validation was performed here, and it does not establish daraxonrasib immune or resistance predictions.
PDAC Immunotherapy PhysiCell Model C++/XML/CSV PhysiCell AGENT_BASED
Grammar-based PhysiCell agent-based PDAC tumor-immune model initialized from PDAC tissue compositions. The model simulates combination therapy with GVAX, nivolumab, and urelumab across heterogeneous baseline microenvironment states using explicit cell-state and interaction rules.

name: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
creation_date: '2026-03-06T00:00:00Z'
description: >-
  Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a malignant pancreatic epithelial neoplasm with ductal
  differentiation. Most tumors harbor an activating KRAS mutation together with alterations in tumor-suppressor
  pathways, but KRAS-wild-type tumors include distinct actionable drivers. Acinar reprogramming,
  ductal-origin models and several precursor lesions contribute to current initiation models; ductal
  morphology does not establish a unique human cell of origin. Desmoplastic fibroblast states, myeloid
  and lymphoid suppression, altered antigen presentation, nutrient scavenging and metabolic adaptation
  shape invasion and treatment response. Resectability and metastatic extent determine clinical management.
  Surgery with systemic therapy offers potential long-term control in selected localized disease;
  advanced disease is treated with systemic regimens and, in defined molecular subsets, targeted
  or immune therapies. Daraxonrasib has randomized clinical efficacy in previously treated metastatic
  PDAC. Its resistance mechanisms now have paired clinical ctDNA evidence, whereas immune-remodeling/checkpoint
  combinations remain preclinical.
categories:
- Solid Tumor
- Gastrointestinal Cancer
- Adenocarcinoma
parents:
- pancreatic cancer
has_subtypes:
- name: Classical Subtype
  description: >-
    An expression program enriched for epithelial differentiation. Classical and basal-like states
    can coexist within a tumor; bulk-expression assignments do not imply immutable, mutually exclusive
    diseases. The original virtual-microdissection cohorts associated classical tumors with better
    survival than basal-like tumors.
  evidence:

    reference_title: Virtual microdissection identifies distinct tumor- and stroma-specific subtypes of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

    evidence_source: COMPUTATIONAL
    snippet: >-

      subtype that has worse outcome and is molecularly similar to basal tumors in
      bladder and breast cancers.
    explanation: >-
      Moffitt et al. used virtual microdissection of gene expression data to identify
      classical and basal-like subtypes of PDAC, with classical having better prognosis.

    A basal/squamous expression program associated with adverse outcome in the original profiling

    and reduced tumors; this is not yet a validated human state-selective treatment.

    involvement. Induction therapy and reassessment guide consideration of surgery.

  description: >-
    Activating KRAS variants favor persistent RAS-GTP signaling through RAF-MEK-ERK and additional
    effector networks, supporting proliferation, survival, metabolic rewiring and microenvironmental
    remodeling. G12D, G12V and G12R are common in PDAC, with allele-specific signaling and inhibitor
    responses. Most PDACs are KRAS-mutant; KRAS-wild-type cancers require separate driver characterization.
    KRAS signaling does not itself establish acquisition of a particular tumor-suppressor mutation
    or therapeutic inhibition.

      PanIN development begins with Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene (KRAS) mutations
      driving PanIN initiation. Key additional mutations in cyclin-dependent kinase

      homolog 4 (SMAD4) disrupt cell cycle control and genomic stability, crucial for
      PanIN progression from low-grade to high-grade dysplasia.
    explanation: >-
      This review confirms KRAS mutations as the initiating event in PanIN development,
      with additional tumor suppressor losses driving progression to invasive carcinoma.

  - target: USP20 Cholesterol-Metabolism CD8 Exhaustion Checkpoint
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      KRAS-G12D induces EGR1-USP20, coordinating cholesterol metabolism and compensatory survival.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:42392864
      reference_title: USP20 promotes CD8(+) T cell exhaustion and impairs KRAS(G12D) inhibitor efficacy by orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Mechanistically, KRASG12D transcriptionally upregulated USP20 via EGR1, which simultaneously deubiquitinated and stabilised 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase and ULK1, thereby orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy-associated survival.
      explanation: >-
        Mechanistic preclinical experiments relate USP20 to cholesterol and autophagy; the cohort
        provides human-tissue context.
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - EGR1-dependent USP20 expression
    - HMG-CoA reductase stabilization
- name: Tumor Suppressor Inactivation
  conforms_to: evading_growth_suppressors#Tumor Suppressor Inactivation
  description: >-
    Alterations of CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 cooperate with oncogenic signaling. Loss of p16 removes
    restraint on CDK4/6-RB cell-cycle progression; p53 alterations weaken stress checkpoints and
    can confer context-dependent gain of function; SMAD4 loss changes TGF-beta responses. Reported
    alteration frequencies differ with cohort, assay, copy-number detection and inclusion of epigenetic
    silencing. These are cooperating events rather than consequences inferred from co-occurrence
    with KRAS.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:18772397
    reference_title: Core signaling pathways in human pancreatic cancers revealed by global genomic analyses.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This list includes the classic tumor suppressor genes CDKN2A (p16), SMAD4,
      and TP53, as well as genes that had not previously been implicated in pancreatic
      cancer development.
    explanation: >-
      The landmark Jones et al. genomic analysis identified CDKN2A, SMAD4, and TP53 as
      core tumor suppressor genes in pancreatic cancer through global sequencing of 24
      advanced pancreatic adenocarcinomas.
  biological_processes:

  downstream:

    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Checkpoint and differentiation defects cooperate with KRAS to permit invasive progression.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26592447
      reference_title: p53 mutations cooperate with oncogenic Kras to promote adenocarcinoma from pancreatic ductal cells.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: In contrast to the lack of response to oncogenic Kras alone, simultaneous activation of Kras and mutant p53 in adult ductal epithelium generated invasive PDAC in 75% of mice as early as 2.5 months after tamoxifen administration.
      explanation: >-
        Cooperating oncogenic KRAS and mutant p53 enable invasive cancer in ductal-origin mice.
- name: Pancreatic Precursor Progression and Invasive Growth
  description: >-
    KRAS-mutant PanIN can progress with cooperating genetic and microenvironmental changes to invasive,
    gland-forming PDAC. IPMN and mucinous cystic neoplasms provide additional precursor routes. Not
    every precursor progresses, and a uniform obligatory mutation order or exclusive acinar origin
    is not established.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:17349585
    reference_title: Chronic pancreatitis is essential for induction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by K-Ras oncogenes in adult mice.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: However, if these mice are challenged with a mild form of chronic pancreatitis, they develop the full spectrum of PanINs and invasive PDA.
    explanation: >-
      Genetic and inflammatory cooperation supports progression in the defined mouse model.
  - reference: PMID:26592447
    reference_title: p53 mutations cooperate with oncogenic Kras to promote adenocarcinoma from pancreatic ductal cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: In contrast to the lack of response to oncogenic Kras alone, simultaneous activation of Kras and mutant p53 in adult ductal epithelium generated invasive PDAC in 75% of mice as early as 2.5 months after tamoxifen administration.
    explanation: >-
      Cooperating oncogenic KRAS and mutant p53 enable invasive cancer in ductal-origin mice.
  downstream:
  - target: Desmoplastic Stroma
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Tumor-secreted ligands promote fibroblast-state changes and matrix-producing stroma.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30366930
      reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Here, we use organoid and mouse models to identify TGFβ and IL1 as tumor-secreted ligands that promote CAF heterogeneity.
      explanation: >-
        Tumor-secreted signals establish heterogeneous stromal responses.
  - target: Metastatic Dissemination and Colonization
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Invasive growth enables dissemination, but the timing and route vary across tumors.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:25985394
      reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Here, we show that PDAC-derived exosomes induce liver pre-metastatic niche formation in naive mice and consequently increase liver metastatic burden.
      explanation: >-
        The primary study experimentally connects extracellular vesicles to a permissive liver niche.
  - target: IL1-LIF-JAK-STAT Inflammatory Fibroblast Programming
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - Tumor-derived IL1α secretion
    - Fibroblast IL1R1 signaling and LIF induction
    description: >-
      The neoplastic epithelial compartment can induce inflammatory fibroblast differentiation
      through secreted IL1α in PDAC organoid-stellate-cell systems. This branch represents signals
      from established tumors, not a claim that invasion itself or extracellular matrix deposition
      directly induces every iCAF state; other ligands contribute in vivo.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30366930
      reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: >-
        Levels of the iCAF markers were significantly reduced when PSCs were cultured with IL-1α
        knockout organoids compared to Rosa26-targeted control organoids, while levels of the myCAF
        marker αSMA were significantly increased (Figure 2D).
      explanation: >-
        Genetic deletion in tumor organoids directly tests the epithelial-to-fibroblast signal in
        vitro; the study separately reports incomplete suppression of the inflammatory phenotype after
        tumor IL1α deletion in vivo.
  - target: Tumor-Restraining Fibroblast Programs
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - Tumor-derived SHH secretion
    - Stromal Hedgehog pathway activation and fibroblast expansion
    description: >-
      Neoplastic cells can establish a Hedgehog-responsive fibroblast-rich stroma with
      tumor-restraining activity in a genetically engineered PDAC mouse model. This incoming branch
      concerns the SHH-dependent component of the heterogeneous stromal node, not all fibroblast
      states or a universal protective role for fibrosis.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:24856585
      reference_title: "Stromal elements act to restrain, rather than support, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        Sonic hedgehog (Shh), a soluble ligand overexpressed by neoplastic cells in pancreatic ductal
        adenocarcinoma (PDAC), drives formation of a fibroblast-rich desmoplastic stroma.
      explanation: >-
        The source identifies the tumor-derived ligand and stromal response; the genetic perturbation
        below tests its restraining function in mice.
    - reference: PMID:24856585
      reference_title: "Stromal elements act to restrain, rather than support, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        As predicted, Shh-deficient tumors had reduced stromal content. Surprisingly, such tumors were
        more aggressive and exhibited undifferentiated histology, increased vascularity, and
        heightened proliferation--features that were fully recapitulated in control mice treated with
        a Smoothened inhibitor.
      explanation: >-
        Loss of tumor SHH or pharmacologic Hedgehog inhibition reduced stroma and increased aggressive
        growth in this model. The edge does not equate SHH-driven stroma with every alphaSMA-positive,
        inflammatory or interferon-responsive fibroblast population.
  - target: Pancreatic Exocrine Functional Loss
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - Main pancreatic duct obstruction
    - Gland fibrosis and loss of exocrine tissue
    description: >-
      An established pancreatic tumor can impair exocrine secretion through duct obstruction and
      loss of functional tissue. Risk depends on tumor location and extent; this is not an
      obligatory consequence of a noninvasive precursor, and postoperative insufficiency has an
      additional surgical cause.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32631175
      reference_title: "Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: >-
        PEI seems to be one of the determinant factors of malnutrition in APC due to obstruction of
        the main pancreatic duct, fibrosis of the gland and loss of pancreatic exocrine tissue.
      explanation: >-
        The systematic review describes the anatomic mechanisms of exocrine insufficiency in advanced
        pancreatic cancer in its background; the pooled prevalence is not evidence that every
        precursor causes insufficiency.
  - target: Obstructive Jaundice
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - Biliary obstruction from a pancreatic head tumor
    description: >-
      An obstructive pancreatic head cancer can impair bile drainage and cause jaundice. This
      location-dependent consequence of established tumor growth is not attributed to all PDAC or to
      noninvasive precursors.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41067164
      reference_title: "Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with pancreatic cancer."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: >-
        in case of jaundice due to an obstructive head pancreatic cancer, imaging should be carried
        out before biliary drainage or stenting
      explanation: >-
        The guideline explicitly identifies jaundice due to an obstructive pancreatic head cancer and
        recommends imaging before drainage. This supports the anatomic causal route without estimating
        its frequency.
- name: Desmoplastic Stroma
  description: >-
    Tumor-derived signals and local tissue interactions recruit and alter fibroblast states that
    deposit collagen, hyaluronan and other extracellular matrix. Dense matrix can impair perfusion,
    but stromal programs are heterogeneous: some support inflammation or immune exclusion and others
    restrain tumor growth. Fibroblast depletion and matrix digestion are not interchangeable, and
    neither is a generally validated treatment for PDAC.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30366930
    reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Here, we use organoid and mouse models to identify TGFβ and IL1 as tumor-secreted ligands that promote CAF heterogeneity.
    explanation: >-
      Tumor-secreted signals establish heterogeneous stromal responses.

  downstream:
  - target: CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      The FAP-positive CXCL12-producing subset supports spatial immune exclusion.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:24277834
      reference_title: Targeting CXCL12 from FAP-expressing carcinoma-associated fibroblasts synergizes with anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Administering AMD3100, a CXCL12 receptor chemokine (C-X-C motif) receptor 4 inhibitor, induced rapid T-cell accumulation among cancer cells and acted synergistically with α-PD-L1 to greatly diminish cancer cells
      explanation: >-
        Perturbation supports CXCL12-CXCR4-mediated immune exclusion in a mouse PDAC model.
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - FAP-positive fibroblast CXCL12 secretion
    - CXCR4-dependent T-cell exclusion
  - target: Matrix-Associated Hypoperfusion
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Matrix accumulation can impair vascular perfusion.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:22439937
      reference_title: Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: We show here that this desmoplastic reaction generates inordinately high interstitial fluid pressures (IFPs), exceeding those previously measured or theorized for solid tumors, and induces vascular collapse, while presenting substantial barriers to perfusion, diffusion, and convection of small molecule therapeutics.
      explanation: >-
        Primary mouse study supports a physical stromal barrier.
- name: CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
  description: >-
    FAP-positive fibroblasts can supply CXCL12 that localizes around malignant cells and limits T-cell
    access. In KPC mouse tumors, CXCR4 inhibition rapidly increased T-cell accumulation and synergized
    with PD-L1 blockade. This identifies a specific stromal immune-exclusion circuit, not uniform
    behavior of all fibroblasts.

- name: IL1-LIF-JAK-STAT Inflammatory Fibroblast Programming
  description: >-
    Tumor-derived IL1 induces fibroblast LIF and JAK-STAT signaling, promoting an inflammatory CAF
    state. TGF-beta antagonizes this program by reducing IL1R1 and favoring myofibroblasts. Spatial
    exposure and plasticity generate distinct CAF niches, so fibroblast number alone is an inadequate
    mechanistic readout.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30366930
    reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We show that IL1 induces LIF expression and downstream JAK/STAT activation to generate inflammatory CAFs and demonstrate that TGFβ antagonizes this process by downregulating IL1R1 expression and promoting differentiation into myofibroblasts.
    explanation: >-
      Directly distinguishes competing CAF programs.
- name: Tumor-Restraining Fibroblast Programs
  description: >-
    Some fibroblast and stromal programs constrain PDAC. Genetic SHH loss and depletion of alpha-SMA-positive
    myofibroblasts in distinct mouse models accelerated aggressive disease; newer interferon-response
    CAF work also identifies a restraining state. These findings qualify global stroma-removal strategies
    without proving that every myofibroblast state is protective.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24856585
    reference_title: Stromal elements act to restrain, rather than support, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Together, these data demonstrate that some components of the tumor stroma can act to restrain tumor growth.
    explanation: >-
      The primary genetic stromal-perturbation study establishes an important counterexample to uniformly
      tumor-promoting stroma.
  - reference: PMID:24856586
    reference_title: Depletion of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts and fibrosis induces immunosuppression and accelerates pancreas cancer with reduced survival.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Suppressed immune surveillance with increased CD4(+)Foxp3(+) Tregs was observed in myofibroblast-depleted mouse tumors.
    explanation: >-
      Myofibroblast depletion worsened mouse disease; intervention and source scope are explicit.
- name: Matrix-Associated Hypoperfusion
  description: >-
    Hyaluronan-rich stroma can elevate interstitial fluid pressure, collapse vessels and restrict
    delivery of nutrients and drugs in PDAC mouse models. Matrix degradation improved perfusion experimentally,
    but the phase III PEGPH20 trial did not improve survival, limiting direct therapeutic extrapolation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22439937
    reference_title: Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: We show here that this desmoplastic reaction generates inordinately high interstitial fluid pressures (IFPs), exceeding those previously measured or theorized for solid tumors, and induces vascular collapse, while presenting substantial barriers to perfusion, diffusion, and convection of small molecule therapeutics.
    explanation: >-
      Primary mouse study supports a physical stromal barrier.
- name: KRAS-Dependent Anabolic Glucose Metabolism
  description: >-
    KRAS supports glucose uptake and redirects intermediates toward anabolic pathways that sustain
    pancreatic tumor growth. This is a regulated metabolic program rather than a universal switch
    eliminating oxidative phosphorylation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22541435
    reference_title: Oncogenic Kras maintains pancreatic tumors through regulation of anabolic glucose metabolism.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Transcriptome and metabolomic analyses indicate that Kras(G12D) serves a vital role in controlling tumor metabolism through stimulation of glucose uptake and channeling of glucose intermediates into the hexosamine biosynthesis and pentose phosphate pathways (PPP).
    explanation: >-
      Genetic KRAS withdrawal and metabolic profiling establish the growth-supporting program.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: glycolytic process
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0006096
      label: glycolytic process
  downstream:
  - target: Pancreatic Precursor Progression and Invasive Growth
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Nutrient use and redox support permit continued malignant growth.

      explanation: >-

- name: KRAS-Regulated Glutamine Redox Metabolism
  description: >-
    In studied PDAC cells, glutamine-derived aspartate is routed through cytosolic GOT1, malate and
    pyruvate to support NADPH-dependent redox balance. Dependency varies with growth context and
    compensatory metabolism; this does not establish clinical efficacy of glutaminase inhibition.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23535601
    reference_title: Glutamine supports pancreatic cancer growth through a KRAS-regulated metabolic pathway.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Furthermore, we establish that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism is mediated by oncogenic KRAS
    explanation: >-
      Genetic experiments connect KRAS to the noncanonical glutamine pathway.

- name: Macropinocytic Protein Scavenging
  description: >-
    RAS-driven macropinocytosis internalizes extracellular protein for lysosomal proteolysis and
    amino-acid supply. It supports growth in nutrient-poor settings and is observed in primary human
    PDAC specimens, complementing transport of free nutrients.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23665962
    reference_title: Macropinocytosis of protein is an amino acid supply route in Ras-transformed cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: The internalized protein undergoes proteolytic degradation, yielding amino acids including glutamine that can enter central carbon metabolism.
    explanation: >-
      Protein uptake supplies usable metabolites in Ras-transformed cellular models.
  - reference: PMID:25644265
    reference_title: Human pancreatic cancer tumors are nutrient poor and tumor cells actively scavenge extracellular protein.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Consistent with this hypothesis, active macropinocytosis is observed in primary human PDAC specimens.
    explanation: >-
      Human tissue supports relevance, without establishing universal flux or dependency.

- name: Autophagy-Lysosome Growth Support
  description: >-
    Basal autophagy can maintain oxidative metabolism and restrain damaging reactive oxygen species
    in established pancreatic cancer models. Recycling also provides substrates under treatment stress.
    The effects of autophagy loss differ by tumor stage and genetic context; preclinical dependency
    is not a validated universal treatment response.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21406549
    reference_title: Pancreatic cancers require autophagy for tumor growth.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of autophagy leads to increased reactive oxygen species, elevated DNA damage, and a metabolic defect leading to decreased mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.
    explanation: >-
      Direct perturbation demonstrates metabolic support in the tested PDAC cells.
  biological_processes:

- name: Immune Evasion
  description: >-
    Myeloid suppression, dysfunctional lymphocytes, stromal exclusion and impaired antigen presentation
    limit immune control in most PDAC. These mechanisms vary between tumors and metastatic sites.
    Rare mismatch-repair-deficient/MSI-high cancers can respond to checkpoint blockade; PDAC is not
    uniformly refractory to every immune or targeted therapy.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1186/s12943-023-01813-y
    reference_title: Molecular and metabolic regulation of immunosuppression in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Immunosuppression is a hallmark of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC),
      contributing to early metastasis and poor patient survival.
    explanation: >-
      This review establishes immunosuppression as a hallmark of PDAC that contributes
      to metastasis and poor survival, supporting the immune evasion mechanism.
  - reference: DOI:10.1186/s12943-023-01813-y
    reference_title: Molecular and metabolic regulation of immunosuppression in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Following chemokine and exosomal guidance, these cells metastasize to the
      organ-specific pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) constituted by local resident cells,
      stromal fibroblasts, and suppressive immune cells, such as the metastasis-associated
      macrophages, neutrophils, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells.
    explanation: >-
      This describes the immune cell populations in PDAC metastatic niches including
      macrophages, neutrophils, and MDSCs that constitute the immunosuppressive
      microenvironment.

- name: KRAS-GM-CSF Myeloid Immunosuppression
  description: >-
    Oncogenic KRAS induces tumor-cell GM-CSF, expanding suppressive myeloid cells that constrain
    cytotoxic T-cell immunity in pancreatic neoplasia models. This supplies a disease-driving counterpart
    to the myeloid remodeling seen after KRAS inhibition.
  evidence:

    reference_title: Oncogenic Kras-induced GM-CSF production promotes the development of pancreatic neoplasia.

- name: NBR1-Mediated MHC-I Autophagic Degradation
  description: >-
    Selective autophagy directs MHC-I to lysosomes through NBR1, reducing surface antigen presentation
    and immune recognition in PDAC models. Autophagy inhibition can restore MHC-I and improve T-cell
    control. This can coexist with RAS-dependent and FAK-dependent regulation; pathway dominance
    or mutual independence has not been established.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32376951
    reference_title: Autophagy promotes immune evasion of pancreatic cancer by degrading MHC-I.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Here we show that, in PDAC, MHC-I molecules are selectively targeted for lysosomal degradation by an autophagy-dependent mechanism that involves the autophagy cargo receptor NBR1.
    explanation: >-
      Primary study establishes selective antigen-presentation loss through autophagy.

- name: FAK-Mediated Antigen-Presentation Suppression
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Tumor-cell FAK signaling limits immunoproteasome expression and antigen presentation in PDAC
    models. FAK depletion increases antigen diversity and MHC-I presentation; combined STAT3 loss
    further promotes immune control. This is a complementary regulator, not evidence that RAS cannot
    influence MHC-I. The reported antigen-presentation effect is kinase-independent, requires nuclear
    FAK, and is lost in an extreme squamous phenotype; FAK kinase inhibition is therefore not equivalent
    to eliminating this function.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36977556
    reference_title: FAK suppresses antigen processing and presentation to promote immune evasion in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Loss of PDAC cell-intrinsic FAK signalling promotes expression of the immunoproteasome and Major Histocompatibility Complex class-I (MHC-I), resulting in increased antigen diversity and antigen presentation by FAK-/- PDAC cells.
    explanation: >-
      The primary study evaluates FAK-dependent immune regulation in pancreatic cancer models.

- name: Exosome-MIF Liver Premetastatic Niche
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    PDAC-derived exosomes carrying MIF can be taken up by Kupffer cells, inducing TGF-beta, hepatic
    stellate-cell fibronectin deposition and recruitment of bone-marrow-derived macrophages. This
    establishes a liver premetastatic niche mechanism; the cited study does not by itself establish
    direct exosomal suppression of dendritic cells or T cells.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25985394
    reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Uptake of PDAC-derived exosomes by Kupffer cells caused transforming growth factor
      β secretion and upregulation of fibronectin production by hepatic stellate cells.
      This fibrotic microenvironment enhanced recruitment of bone marrow-derived
      macrophages.
    explanation: >-
      The primary study supports exosomal MIF-driven liver niche formation and metastasis, not direct
      proof of lymphocyte suppression.
  - reference: PMID:25985394
    reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      We found that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was highly expressed in
      PDAC-derived exosomes, and its blockade prevented liver pre-metastatic niche
      formation and metastasis.
    explanation: >-
      The primary study supports exosomal MIF-driven liver niche formation and metastasis, not direct
      proof of lymphocyte suppression.

- name: Metastatic Dissemination and Colonization
  description: >-
    Invasive tumor cells disseminate and establish distant lesions, frequently in the liver and also
    lung or peritoneum. Colonization depends on both tumor-cell programs and organ-specific niches;
    metastatic-site immune composition differs from the primary tumor. A single EMT program is not
    obligatory for every metastatic event.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25985394
    reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Here, we show that PDAC-derived exosomes induce liver pre-metastatic niche formation in naive mice and consequently increase liver metastatic burden.
    explanation: >-
      The primary study experimentally connects extracellular vesicles to a permissive liver niche.
  downstream:
  - target: Hepatic Metastases
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Hepatic colonization is a common site-specific manifestation among patients presenting with
      metastatic PDAC.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36776324
      reference_title: A population-based study of synchronous distant metastases and prognosis in patients with PDAC at initial diagnosis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        There was a highest incidence of liver metastases from pancreatic cancer
        (2387,74.36%), followed by lung (625,19.47%), bone (190,5.92%), and brain
        (8,0.25%).
      explanation: >-
        This population-based study of metastatic PDAC directly identifies liver
        metastases as the most common distant metastatic site at diagnosis.
- name: Early Dissemination and EMT
  conforms_to: invasion_and_metastasis#Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition Activation
  description: >-
    Epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity can accompany dissemination and drug resistance, but individual
    EMT transcription factors have nonredundant roles. Snail or Twist deletion did not abolish metastasis
    in a KPC study. Early dissemination observed in mouse precursor models is not proof that all
    human PDAC metastasizes before invasion.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22265420
    reference_title: EMT and dissemination precede pancreatic tumor formation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Tagged cells invaded and entered the bloodstream unexpectedly early, before frank malignancy could be detected by rigorous histologic analysis; this behavior was widely associated with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
    explanation: >-
      Lineage tracking establishes early dissemination in a mouse pancreatic-cancer model, not universal
      timing of human metastasis.
  - reference: PMID:26560028
    reference_title: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition is dispensable for metastasis but induces chemoresistance in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: EMT suppression in the primary tumour does not alter the emergence of invasive PDAC, systemic dissemination or metastasis.
    explanation: >-
      Snail/Twist deletion challenges obligatory EMT in this mouse model; it does not show that all
      EMT programs are irrelevant.

- name: Perineural Invasion
  description: >-
    Pancreatic cancer cells interact with nerves and migrate along neural structures. HGF-MET signaling
    can activate mTOR-NGF, promoting nerve recruitment and invasion in experimental models. PNI is
    associated with adverse clinical outcomes and can contribute to pain; it is not established as
    the universal route to distant metastasis. Human NGF/TrkA levels correlate with PNI and pain
    in one tissue cohort, but a prospective resectable cohort found pain did not predict PNI; clinical
    pain and neural invasion are not interchangeable readouts.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35449152
    reference_title: HGF/c-Met pathway facilitates the perineural invasion of pancreatic cancer by activating the mTOR/NGF axis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Activating the HGF/c-Met signaling pathway potentiated the expression of nerve growth factor (NGF) to recruit nerves and promote the PNI.
    explanation: >-
      Direct perturbation supports tumor-nerve crosstalk.
  - reference: PMID:35449152
    reference_title: HGF/c-Met pathway facilitates the perineural invasion of pancreatic cancer by activating the mTOR/NGF axis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: we found that knocking down c-Met expression inhibited cancer cell migration along the nerve, reduced the damage of the sciatic nerve caused by cancer cells and protected the function of the sciatic nerve in vivo.
    explanation: >-
      Mouse nerve-invasion experiments support local injury, not a clinical pain-frequency estimate.
  - reference: PMID:10561305
    reference_title: Nerve growth factor expression correlates with perineural invasion and pain in human pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Enhanced expression of the NGF/TrkA system may influence perineural invasion and may contribute to the pain syndrome in human pancreatic cancer.
    explanation: >-
      Human tissue association supports biological relevance while preserving the authors causal
      uncertainty.
  - reference: PMID:28785934
    reference_title: Prospective Evaluation of Associations between Cancer-Related Pain and Perineural Invasion in Patients with Resectable Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Preoperative pain does not predict the presence of perineural invasion or other pathologic prognostic factors in patients with resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
    explanation: >-
      Prospective 52-patient resectable cohort qualifies pain as a neural-invasion surrogate.

    term:
      id: GO:0030335
      label: positive regulation of cell migration
- name: Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    In immunocompetent PDAC models, RAS(ON) multiselective inhibition can reduce suppressive myeloid
    subsets, increase tumor MHC-I and lymphocyte infiltration, and enable immune-dependent tumor
    control. RMC-7977 and daraxonrasib provide direct PDAC evidence. Responses and optimal checkpoint
    partners are model-dependent; increased Tregs and adaptive myeloid rebound can limit benefit.
    Patient survival from daraxonrasib monotherapy does not establish an immune-mediated clinical
    benefit.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40057911
    reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.
    explanation: >-
      Direct PDAC evidence was omitted from the immune report despite being cited in the resistance
      report.
  - reference: PMID:40057911
    reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: The depth and duration of tumor regression depended on T cells and conventional dendritic cells.
    explanation: >-
      Depletion/genetic experiments establish immune contribution in mouse PDAC.
- name: Cyclophilin A Loss and Reduced Tri-Complex Engagement
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    A preprint reports reduced cyclophilin-A protein with retained KRAS-G12D-GTP signaling in daraxonrasib-resistant
    PDAC cells. As cyclophilin A is required for tri-complex formation, reduced availability is a
    plausible drug-engagement escape mechanism. This observation does not establish that peptidyl-prolyl
    isomerase catalytic activity was measured or is causally required. The single clinical case in
    this paper instead concerns KRAS-G12R EGFR/wild-type-RAS activation.

    evidence_source: IN_VITRO

    explanation: >-

- name: RAS-Independent Cell-Cycle Uncoupling
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    A preprint describes acquired RMC-6236 resistance in mixed PDAC and NSCLC models with sustained
    cell-cycle progression despite RAS suppression. CDK4/6 or CDK2 cotargeting restored control through
    distinct arrest programs; CDK2 inhibition produced more durable cytostasis in the tested settings.
    This is not a clinically validated combination or proof that simultaneous inhibition of all three
    kinases is required. CDK8-mediated microenvironmental resistance is a separate mechanism.
  biological_processes:

    modifier: INCREASED

      label: cell population proliferation

    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: While these pathways can be broadly inhibited using the pan-RAS-ON inhibitor RMC-6236, cells remained capable of developing acquired resistance where cell proliferation is uncoupled from RAS signaling.
    explanation: >-

- name: Acquired RAS(ON) Inhibitor Resistance
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    Daraxonrasib can initially control PDAC and subsequently lose efficacy through heterogeneous
    resistance routes. An August 2026 study profiled 44 patients with response or stable disease
    lasting more than three months followed by progression: 59% had treatment-emergent RAS-pathway
    genomic alterations, including KRAS amplification in 36%. Mutant-allele identity was inferred from
    variant-allele-frequency ratios by an exploratory method, not directly confirmed in all cases.
    These selected-cohort findings establish patient mechanisms but not universal resistance or population-wide route frequencies.
    Median progression-free survival alone cannot distinguish acquired resistance, primary nonresponse
    and death. Non-genomic, tissue-specific and low-shedding routes remain incompletely captured.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Here we report mechanisms of acquired resistance to daraxonrasib monotherapy observed through targeted sequencing of over 800 genes in paired pretreatment and end of treatment circulating tumor DNA samples from 44 patients in the phase 1/2 clinical trial.
    explanation: >-
      August 2026 paired clinical sequencing supersedes the July reports and earlier assessment claim
      that no longitudinal clinical characterization was available.
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.
    explanation: >-
      Frequencies apply to 44 profiled patients with prior disease control followed by progression,
      not all treated PDAC patients; categories overlap. Mutant-allele attribution from ctDNA is
      exploratory and unconfirmed, as specified in Supplementary Table 3.
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Notably, no acquired secondary KRAS mutations were observed, distinct from resistance profiles of mutant-selective KRAS G12C(OFF) inhibitors.
    explanation: >-
      No secondary KRAS mutations were found in this selected PDAC cohort; this is not proof that
      such mutations are impossible.
- name: On-Target RAS Reactivation and KRAS Amplification
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    Increased mutant KRAS dosage can attenuate daraxonrasib suppression and restore RAS-pathway
    output in PDAC models. Paired ctDNA detected emergent KRAS amplification in 16/44 profiled PDAC
    patients after initial disease control. Assignment to the pre-existing mutant allele was inferred
    from variant-allele-frequency ratios; the supplementary table explicitly calls this exploratory
    and unconfirmed, rather than direct allele phasing in all cases. Engineered and selected PDAC
    models provide functional corroboration of mutant KRAS dosage. Secondary KRAS mutations were
    absent from the 44 PDAC cases and selected PDAC resistance models, while an engineered Ba/F3
    deep mutational scan identified resistance-conferring second-site variants in a different context.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.
    explanation: >-
      Frequencies apply to 44 profiled patients with prior disease control followed by progression,
      not all treated PDAC patients; categories overlap. Mutant-allele attribution from ctDNA is
      exploratory and unconfirmed, as specified in Supplementary Table 3.
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Method is exploratory, and allele amplification is not confirmed.
    explanation: >-
      Supplementary Table 3 qualifies mutant-versus-wild-type assignment from relative variant allele
      frequencies. This limitation does not negate the observed 16/44 KRAS amplification calls.
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: To corroborate these clinical findings, we found, or mechanistically established, concordant mechanisms of daraxonrasib resistance in human and murine preclinical models of PDAC, including mutant KRAS and MYC amplification and RTK upregulation, with these alterations guiding various combination therapy concepts.
    explanation: >-
      Preclinical perturbation corroborates selected clinical candidate routes; it does not establish
      causality for every observed co-alteration.

      explanation: >-

    - ras_on_inhibitor_acquired_resistance
  notes: >-
    No causal edge from initiating KRAS activation to acquired KRAS amplification is asserted.

- name: RTK and Feedback Pathway Reactivation
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    RTK signaling can contribute to daraxonrasib resistance in particular PDAC contexts. The paired
    44-patient study found emergent RTK alterations in 4/44, with HER2-upregulated resistant models
    providing functional support. A separate preprint identified EGFR/wild-type-RAS activation in
    KRAS-G12R models and one patient who progressed after ten months. G12D cyclophilin-A loss is
    a distinct route. Earlier MEK or G12C-selective-inhibitor studies are contextual analogies and
    do not establish universal sufficiency against multiselective inhibition.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.
    explanation: >-
      Frequencies apply to 44 profiled patients with prior disease control followed by progression,
      not all treated PDAC patients; categories overlap. Mutant-allele attribution from ctDNA is
      exploratory and unconfirmed, as specified in Supplementary Table 3.
  - reference: PMID:42465401
    reference_title: 'Overcoming Daraxonrasib Resistance: Allele-Specific Mechanisms Guide Salvage Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: KRAS G12R is marked by its inability to transactivate RAS WT , and it was observed that daraxonrasib resistant KRAS G12R PDAC cells utilize EGFR/RAS WT -GTP signaling as the dominant adaptive route.
    explanation: >-
      Preprint supports an allele-specific cellular route; it should not be generalized to all KRAS
      alleles.
