- name: Adaptive mTOR and JUN-AP1 Transcriptional Program
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    CRISPR screens identify mTOR and JUN as convergent mediators of resistance to MAPK-pathway inhibitor
    combinations. In PDAC cells, JUN overexpression supported resistance to SHP2 plus RMC-6236; in-vivo
    MAP2K4 rescue used SHP2 plus ERK inhibition. The combination-specific evidence should not be
    recast as patient-level daraxonrasib monotherapy resistance. A separate RMC-7977 mouse study
    identified focal Jun gain in one resistant tumor.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41572361
    reference_title: CRISPR knockout screens reveal JUN as the master mediator of resistance to MAPK inhibition in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Through unbiased CRISPR-based screenings, we identified mTOR and JUN hyperactivation as interconnected mechanisms that overcome MAPK suppression.
    explanation: >-
      CRISPR and follow-up cellular experiments support the combination-treatment scope.

    reference_title: CRISPR knockout screens reveal JUN as the master mediator of resistance to MAPK inhibition in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.

- name: Mitochondrial Remodeling and Ferroptosis Vulnerability
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    Dual SHP2-MEK inhibition produces persistent mitochondrial changes and lipid-peroxide-defense
    dependency in PDAC models, with confirmation under direct RAS targeting. Sensitivity to GPX4
    disruption is an exploitable treatment-induced vulnerability; it does not mean ferroptosis is
    already increased or that this state itself causes clinical daraxonrasib resistance. The primary
    intervention and model context are retained.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41545339
    reference_title: Vertical RAS pathway inhibition in pancreatic cancer drives therapeutically exploitable mitochondrial alterations.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We found that dual SHP2/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK1/2) inhibition induces major alterations in mitochondrial mass and function, impacts reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis and triggers lipid peroxidase dependency.
    explanation: >-
      The primary experiment concerns vertical SHP2-MEK blockade.
- name: MYC Amplification-Driven RAS-Independent Proliferation
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    RMC-7977-resistant KPC tumors frequently gained Myc copies while maintaining ERK suppression.
    YAP-TEAD-dependent transcriptional output accompanied resistance, and TEAD cotargeting restored
    sensitivity in vitro. The subsequent daraxonrasib clinical study detected MYC amplification in
    one patient together with KRAS amplification and corroborated MYC-related resistance in models.
    These data support a bypass route without proving that all MYC gain is independent of RAS or
    that TEAD combinations benefit patients.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38588697
    reference_title: Tumour-selective activity of RAS-GTP inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Analysis of relapsed tumours identified Myc copy number gain as a prevalent candidate resistance mechanism, which could be overcome by combinatorial TEAD inhibition in vitro.
    explanation: >-
      Primary 2024 RMC-7977 study supplies stronger support than the systematic review cited by OpenScientist.
  - reference: PMID:42581230
    reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: We also observed truncating mutations in NF1 (2 of 44; 4%), KEAP1 (2 of 44; 4%), a PTPN11 mutation or MYC amplification in one patient each (1 of 44; 2%).
    explanation: >-

      attribution.

- name: Myeloid Suppression Relief and CD8 Effector Infiltration
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    MRTX1133 and RAS(ON) multiselective inhibitors can reduce suppressive myeloid subsets and increase
    effector lymphocytes in immunocompetent PDAC models. Total macrophage abundance can increase
    while state composition changes; myeloid remodeling is not equivalent to depletion of every myeloid
    cell. The direction and durability of individual populations vary by agent, model and time.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: CD8-positive effector T cell
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: CL:0000625
      label: CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40057911
    reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.
    explanation: >-
      Direct PDAC evidence was omitted from the immune report despite being cited in the resistance
      report.
  - reference: PMID:37625401
    reference_title: KRAS(G12D) inhibition reprograms the microenvironment of early and advanced pancreatic cancer to promote FAS-mediated killing by CD8(+) T cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: MRTX1133 reverses early PDAC growth, increases intratumoral CD8+ effector T cells, decreases myeloid infiltration, and reprograms cancer-associated fibroblasts.
    explanation: >-
      Final peer-reviewed MRTX1133 paper; its preprint PMID36824971 is not independent replication.

- name: Tumor-Cell FAS Induction and CD8-Mediated Killing
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    KRAS-G12D inhibition by MRTX1133 induces FAS in malignant cells and patient-derived organoids,
    permitting CD8-mediated killing in PDAC models. This is drug- and model-specific evidence; the
    original citation to the preprint has been replaced with the final paper. CDK8-dependent FAS
    suppression can later oppose this response.

- name: USP20 Cholesterol-Metabolism CD8 Exhaustion Checkpoint
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    KRAS-G12D induces EGR1-USP20, stabilizing HMG-CoA reductase and promoting cholesterol metabolism
    associated with CD8 exhaustion. KRAS inhibition or cholesterol blockade induces compensatory
    ULK1-associated autophagy; USP20 also stabilizes ULK1. This is a two-arm metabolic and survival
    mechanism. MRTX1133 plus USP20 inhibition and PD-1 blockade regressed tumors in preclinical models,
    but human tissue profiling is not evidence of clinical combination efficacy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42392864
    reference_title: USP20 promotes CD8(+) T cell exhaustion and impairs KRAS(G12D) inhibitor efficacy by orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Mechanistically, KRASG12D transcriptionally upregulated USP20 via EGR1, which simultaneously deubiquitinated and stabilised 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase and ULK1, thereby orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy-associated survival.
    explanation: >-
      Mechanistic preclinical experiments relate USP20 to cholesterol and autophagy; the cohort provides
      human-tissue context.
  - reference: PMID:42392864
    reference_title: USP20 promotes CD8(+) T cell exhaustion and impairs KRAS(G12D) inhibitor efficacy by orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: In preclinical PDAC models, triple therapy with GSK2643943A, MRTX1133 and anti-PD-1 elicited a robust therapeutic response and induced significant tumour regression.
    explanation: >-
      Mouse combination activity remains investigational.

- name: CDK8-CXCL2 Adaptive Immune Reversal
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    Long-term MRTX1133 treatment can reverse early immune infiltration through CDK8-associated CXCL2
    secretion and FAS suppression. CDK8 perturbation restores immune control in those PDAC models.
    Daraxonrasib-resistant PDX tumors also show CDK8 upregulation, but this does not establish the
    entire temporal CXCL2/FAS immune circuit under daraxonrasib or in patients.

    supports: SUPPORT

    snippet: CDK8 imparts this resistance via induction of CXCL2 chemokine secretion, inhibition of FAS expression, and remodeling of the TME to promote immune evasion.
    explanation: >-
      The mechanistic immune reversal was tested chiefly during MRTX1133 treatment.

- name: Regulatory T-Cell Recruitment after KRAS Inhibition
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    An August 2026 PDAC study found that MRTX1133 or daraxonrasib recruits regulatory as well as
    effector and exhausted T cells. In its models, CTLA-4 blockade reprogrammed effector Tregs, reduced
    CD8 exhaustion and supported tertiary lymphoid structures. Other checkpoint combinations were
    less effective. This contrasts with a different RMC-7977 model where the CD4 increase was not
    attributable to FoxP3-positive Tregs, so generalized Treg relief is not supported.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75960-3
    reference_title: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Here, we demonstrate that Kras* targeting using MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib recruits diverse T-cell infiltrates, including regulatory (Tregs), effector and exhausted T cells into the PDAC microenvironment.
    explanation: >-
      Newer mouse PDAC evidence replaces the unsupported positive Treg-relief node.
  - reference: PMID:40057911
    reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: the increase in CD4+ T cells upon RMC-7977 treatment was not attributable to this population
    explanation: >-
      In this separate model the CD4 expansion did not reflect FoxP3-positive Tregs, illustrating
      model dependence.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: regulatory T cell
    term:
      id: CL:0000815
      label: regulatory T cell

        Single-cell and perturbation work establishes a counter-regulatory microenvironment under
        SOS1-MEK blockade.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - ras_on_inhibition_immune_tme_remodeling
- name: Basal-State GM-CSF Immunosuppressive Circuit
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Basal malignant cells can organize tumor-maintaining fibroblast, macrophage and cytokine states.
    Lineage tracing found greater plasticity of basal than classical cells in autochthonous mouse
    PDAC. Basal-state ablation, and separately basal-cell GM-CSF knockout, reprogrammed the stroma
    and recruited cytotoxic lymphocytes. This establishes a causal circuit in these models while
    leaving human state-targeting efficacy unresolved.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42523238
    reference_title: The basal cell state maintains pancreatic cancers by controlling an immunosuppressive circuit.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Knockout of a single cytokine, GM-CSF, specifically in basal cells recapitulated macrophage repolarization and lymphocyte recruitment observed upon basal state ablation and shrank tumors.
    explanation: >-
      Basal-cell-specific genetic perturbation establishes an immune-organizing GM-CSF role in mouse
      PDAC. Human prognostic association does not establish the same intervention effect.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CSF2
    term:
      id: hgnc:2434
      label: CSF2
  downstream:
  - target: Immune Evasion
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Basal-cell GM-CSF maintains an immunosuppressive tumor ecosystem in autochthonous mouse PDAC.
    evidence:

      reference_title: The basal cell state maintains pancreatic cancers by controlling an immunosuppressive circuit.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Knockout of a single cytokine, GM-CSF, specifically in basal cells recapitulated macrophage repolarization and lymphocyte recruitment observed upon basal state ablation and shrank tumors.
      explanation: >-
        Basal-cell-specific genetic perturbation establishes an immune-organizing GM-CSF role in
        mouse PDAC. Human prognostic association does not establish the same intervention effect.
- name: Pancreatic Exocrine Functional Loss
  description: >-
    Tumor-associated obstruction and loss of functional pancreatic tissue can impair digestive enzyme
    delivery. The resulting maldigestion contributes to nutritional loss; this process also occurs
    after pancreatic surgery. Clinical prevalence varies with stage, location and testing method.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32631175
    reference_title: 'Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)'
    explanation: >-
      Meta-analysis supports substantial exocrine insufficiency specifically in advanced pancreatic
      cancer; heterogeneity and tumor location limit generalization to all PDAC.
  downstream:
  - target: Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Loss of digestive enzyme delivery produces clinical pancreatic exocrine insufficiency.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32631175
      reference_title: 'Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: 'The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)'
      explanation: >-
        Meta-analysis supports substantial exocrine insufficiency specifically in advanced pancreatic
        cancer; heterogeneity and tumor location limit generalization to all PDAC.
  - target: Weight Loss
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Maldigestion is one contributor to weight loss in advanced pancreatic cancer.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32631175
      reference_title: 'Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.'
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency is one of the causes of malnutrition and weight loss in these patients.
      explanation: >-
        Clinical synthesis identifies this contribution without attributing all weight loss to pancreatic
        insufficiency.
- name: Adaptive CD24 Antiphagocytic Signaling
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    In KRAS-G12C-driven mouse PDAC, selective KRAS inhibition upregulated the CD24 antiphagocytic
    signal despite an inflamed microenvironment. CD24 blockade increased macrophage phagocytosis
    and sensitized tumors; related findings occurred in G12D PDAC. The preprint and final paper report
    the same work. This is a plausible immune-adaptation route whose relevance to clinical daraxonrasib
    progression remains unproven.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40966362
    reference_title: KRAS Inhibition Activates an Actionable CD24 "Do Not Eat Me" Signal in Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Blocking CD24 enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of cancer cells and significantly sensitized tumors to G12Ci treatment.
    explanation: >-
      Functional antibody perturbation supports CD24-mediated adaptation in G12C/G12D-selective-inhibitor
      PDAC models, not a proven clinical daraxonrasib-resistance route.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CD24
    term:
      id: hgnc:1645
      label: CD24
  downstream:
  - target: Immune Evasion
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Induced CD24 reduces macrophage-mediated tumor-cell clearance in selective-KRAS-inhibitor models.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40966362
      reference_title: KRAS Inhibition Activates an Actionable CD24 "Do Not Eat Me" Signal in Pancreatic Cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Blocking CD24 enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of cancer cells and significantly sensitized tumors to G12Ci treatment.
      explanation: >-
        Functional antibody perturbation supports CD24-mediated adaptation in G12C/G12D-selective-inhibitor
        PDAC models, not a proven clinical daraxonrasib-resistance route.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - ras_on_inhibitor_acquired_resistance
    - ras_on_inhibition_immune_tme_remodeling
- name: Senescent Myofibroblast Immunosuppression
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Senescent myofibroblastic CAFs accumulate near tumor ducts and during PDAC progression. Genetic
    or pharmacologic depletion of senescent stromal cells in mouse models reduced macrophage-associated
    immune suppression and improved chemotherapy responsiveness. Human tissue identifies the state,
    but clinical senolytic efficacy is not established.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-0428
    reference_title: Senescence Defines a Distinct Subset of Myofibroblasts That Orchestrates Immunosuppression in Pancreatic Cancer
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Depletion of senescent stromal cells in genetic and pharmacologic PDAC models relieved immune suppression by macrophages, delayed tumor progression, and increased responsiveness to chemotherapy.
    explanation: >-
      Mouse senescent-stroma perturbation supports a specific promoting CAF state, complementary
      to tumor-restraining fibroblast programs.
  downstream:
  - target: Immune Evasion
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Senescent stromal programs maintain macrophage-mediated immune suppression in PDAC models.
    evidence:
    - reference: DOI:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-0428
      reference_title: Senescence Defines a Distinct Subset of Myofibroblasts That Orchestrates Immunosuppression in Pancreatic Cancer
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Depletion of senescent stromal cells in genetic and pharmacologic PDAC models relieved immune suppression by macrophages, delayed tumor progression, and increased responsiveness to chemotherapy.
      explanation: >-
        Mouse senescent-stroma perturbation supports a specific promoting CAF state, complementary
        to tumor-restraining fibroblast programs.

- name: Desmoplastic Stroma
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: desmoplastic stroma
    term:
      id: NCIT:C36178
      label: Fibrotic Stroma Formation
  description: >-

    histopathologic feature of PDAC.
  evidence:

    reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Here, we use organoid and mouse models to identify TGFβ and IL1 as tumor-secreted ligands that promote CAF heterogeneity.
    explanation: >-
      Tumor-secreted signals establish heterogeneous stromal responses.
phenotypes:
- category: Neoplastic

- category: Clinical

    explanation: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

- category: Clinical
  name: New-Onset Diabetes
  description: >-
    New or worsening diabetes can precede PDAC diagnosis. Cancer-associated pancreatogenic diabetes
    is distinct from longstanding type 2 diabetes as a risk factor; its mechanisms are incompletely
    resolved.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28507210
    reference_title: Diabetes, Pancreatogenic Diabetes, and Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      The relationships between diabetes and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
      are complex. Longstanding type 2 diabetes (T2DM) is a risk factor for pancreatic
      cancer, but increasing epidemiological data point to PDAC as also a cause of
      diabetes due to unknown mechanisms.
    explanation: >-
      Andersen et al. establish that PDAC causes new-onset diabetes through unknown
      mechanisms, demonstrating the bidirectional relationship between PDAC and diabetes.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Diabetes mellitus
    term:
      id: HP:0000819
      label: Diabetes mellitus
- category: Clinical
  name: Hepatic Metastases
  description: >-
    Liver is a common metastatic site. The cited registry estimate of 74.36% concerns synchronous
    metastatic cases, not all PDAC or all patients with locally advanced disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36776324
    reference_title: A population-based study of synchronous distant metastases and prognosis in patients with PDAC at initial diagnosis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was a highest incidence of liver metastases from pancreatic cancer
      (2387,74.36%), followed by lung (625,19.47%), bone (190,5.92%), and brain
      (8,0.25%).
    explanation: >-
      This population-based study of metastatic PDAC directly identifies liver
      metastases as the most common distant metastatic site at diagnosis.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hepatic metastasis
    term:

biochemical:
- name: CA 19-9
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23331006
    reference_title: 'The clinical utility of CA 19-9 in pancreatic adenocarcinoma: diagnostic and prognostic updates.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In 57 studies involving 3,285 pancreatic carcinoma cases, the combined
      sensitivity of CA 19-9 was 78.2% and in 37 studies involving 1,882 cases with
      benign pancreatic disease the specificity of CA 19-9 was 82.8%.
    explanation: >-
      Poruk et al. meta-analysis established CA 19-9 sensitivity of 78.2% and
      specificity of 82.8% for pancreatic carcinoma diagnosis.
  notes: >-
    CA 19-9 assists disease-burden and response assessment; the cited diagnostic sensitivity and
    specificity come from pooled clinical studies, not population screening. It cannot independently
    establish or exclude PDAC.
- name: Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA)
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23331006
    reference_title: 'The clinical utility of CA 19-9 in pancreatic adenocarcinoma: diagnostic and prognostic updates.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      From the combined analysis of studies reporting CEA, the sensitivity was
      44.2% (1,324 cases) and the specificity was 84.8% (656 cases).
    explanation: >-
      Poruk et al. meta-analysis showed CEA has lower sensitivity (44.2%) than
      CA 19-9 but comparable specificity (84.8%) for pancreatic carcinoma.
  notes: >-
    CEA is a supplementary marker with lower pooled sensitivity than CA 19-9 and similar specificity
    in the cited analysis. Neither is adequate as a stand-alone screening or diagnostic test.
genetic:
- name: KRAS
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: KRAS
    term:
      id: hgnc:6407
      label: KRAS
  association: Somatic Gain-of-Function Mutation
  inheritance:
  - name: Somatic
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33347393
    reference_title: 'Clinical Effect of Driver Mutations of KRAS, CDKN2A/P16, TP53, and SMAD4 in Pancreatic Cancer: A Meta-Analysis.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: This systematic review and meta-analysis supports the use of driver mutations in the P53, SMAD4, and KRAS genes as prognostic markers for pancreatic cancer.
    explanation: Directly supports KRAS as an established driver mutation and prognostic marker in pancreatic cancer.
  - reference: DOI:10.3389/fmed.2024.1369136
    reference_title: 'Targeting KRAS mutations in pancreatic cancer: opportunities for future strategies'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: In the case of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), 90–92% harbor mutations in the oncogene KRAS, triggering canonical MAPK signaling.
    explanation: >-
      Review-level estimate and signaling background; precise frequencies vary by assay and cohort.
  notes: >-
    Activating KRAS mutations occur in most PDAC and many PanIN precursors; G12D, G12V and G12R are
    common alleles. Frequencies depend on cohort and assay. KRAS-wild-type PDAC requires investigation
    for alternative drivers.
- name: TP53
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: TP53
    term:
      id: hgnc:11998
      label: TP53
  association: Somatic Loss-of-Function Mutation
  inheritance:
  - name: Somatic
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37404765
    reference_title: Genomic landscape of clinically advanced KRAS wild-type pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      the KRAS mutated group had a significantly higher percentage of TP53
      (mutated vs wild-type: 80.2% vs 47.6%, p <0.0001)
    explanation: >-
      Foundation Medicine genomic profiling of 9,444 advanced PDAC cases showed TP53
      mutations in 80.2% of KRAS-mutated PDAC.
  notes: >-
    Somatic TP53 disruption cooperates with oncogenic signaling and impairs damage responses. The
    cited advanced-disease profiling cohort reported 80.2% in KRAS-mutated versus 47.6% in KRAS-wild-type
    tumors; these are cohort-specific alteration rates.

    reference_title: Core signaling pathways in human pancreatic cancers revealed by global genomic analyses.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: This list includes the classic tumor suppressor genes CDKN2A (p16), SMAD4, and TP53, as well as genes that had not previously been implicated in pancreatic cancer development.
    explanation: Directly identifies CDKN2A/p16 as a classic tumor suppressor gene affected by homozygous deletion in pancreatic cancers.
  - reference: PMID:37404765
    reference_title: Genomic landscape of clinically advanced KRAS wild-type pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      CDKN2A (mutated vs wild-type: 56.2% vs 34.4%, p <0.0001)
    explanation: >-
      Clinical profiling reports different CDKN2A alteration rates between KRAS strata; it does not
      quantify promoter silencing.
  notes: >-
    Somatic p16-pathway loss can arise through mutation, deletion or silencing and removes CDK4/6
    restraint. These mechanisms should not be assigned a combined frequency from a mutation-only
    assay.
- name: BRCA2
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: BRCA2
    term:
      id: hgnc:1101
      label: BRCA2
  association: Inherited predisposition and somatic homologous-recombination deficiency
  inheritance:
  - name: Autosomal dominant
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31157963
    reference_title: Maintenance Olaparib for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Patients with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation make up a small subgroup of
      those with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The poly(adenosine diphosphate-ribose)
      polymerase (PARP) inhibitor olaparib has had antitumor activity in this population.
    explanation: >-
      The POLO trial confirmed that BRCA-mutated PDAC patients represent a distinct
      subgroup that responds to PARP inhibition, validating the clinical relevance
      of BRCA2 mutations in PDAC.
  notes: >-
    Germline pathogenic variants confer inherited cancer susceptibility; tumor biallelic loss can
    cause homologous-recombination deficiency. Somatic alterations also occur. POLO evidence specifically
    concerns germline BRCA1/2 metastatic cases without progression on platinum.

    reference_title: 'Factors that affect risk for pancreatic disease in the general population: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Current tobacco use was the single most important risk factor for pancreatic
      diseases (RR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.54-2.27)
    explanation: >-
      Meta-analysis of 51 population-based prospective cohort studies
      identified tobacco use as the single most important modifiable risk
      factor for pancreatic diseases with an RR of 1.87. The outcome measured
      is pancreatic diseases as a class, and the same abstract reports that
      tobacco has a bigger effect on acute and chronic pancreatitis than on
      pancreatic cancer, so this figure is not a cancer-specific estimate.
- name: Obesity
  description: >-
    Obesity associates with pancreatic disease and is addressed in pancreatic-cancer prevention guidance.
    The cited pooled pancreatic-disease estimate is not specific to PDAC and does not isolate diet
    or a molecular route.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24509242
    reference_title: 'Factors that affect risk for pancreatic disease in the general population: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      followed by obesity (RR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.15-1.92)
    explanation: >-
      Meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies identified obesity as the
      second most important risk factor for pancreatic diseases with an RR of 1.48.
treatments:
- name: Surgical Resection
  description: >-
    Resection offers potential long-term disease control in appropriately selected localized PDAC.
    Pancreaticoduodenectomy treats head lesions; distal pancreatectomy treats body/tail lesions.
    Multidisciplinary staging and perioperative or postoperative systemic therapy determine management.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28129987
    reference_title: 'Comparison of adjuvant gemcitabine and capecitabine with gemcitabine monotherapy in patients with resected pancreatic cancer (ESPAC-4): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older and had undergone complete
      macroscopic resection for ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreas (R0 or R1
      resection).
    explanation: >-
      The ESPAC-4 trial enrolled patients who underwent complete macroscopic resection
      for PDAC, confirming surgical resection as a standard treatment approach with
      adjuvant chemotherapy improving outcomes.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pancreatectomy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15294
      label: Pancreatectomy
- name: FOLFIRINOX Chemotherapy
  description: >-
    Combination of fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan, and oxaliplatin. Used as
    first-line treatment for metastatic PDAC in fit patients and as adjuvant therapy
    after surgical resection. Provides superior survival compared to gemcitabine
    alone but with greater toxicity.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30575490
    reference_title: FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Adjuvant therapy with a modified FOLFIRINOX regimen led to significantly longer
      survival than gemcitabine among patients with resected pancreatic cancer, at the
      expense of a higher incidence of toxic effects.
    explanation: >-
      The PRODIGE 24 trial demonstrated that adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX significantly
      improved disease-free and overall survival compared to gemcitabine in resected
      PDAC patients.
  - reference: PMID:21561347
    reference_title: FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine for metastatic pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The median overall survival was 11.1 months in the FOLFIRINOX group as compared with 6.8 months in the gemcitabine group
    explanation: >-
      Randomized metastatic trial in patients with ECOG performance status 0 or 1 supports first-line
      use in fit patients, separately from the adjuvant trial.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
  regimen_term:
    preferred_term: modified FOLFIRINOX regimen
    term:
      id: NCIT:C11764
      label: Folfirinox Regimen
- name: Gemcitabine-Based Chemotherapy
  description: >-
    Gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel improves survival over gemcitabine alone in metastatic PDAC,
    with increased neuropathy and myelosuppression. Regimen selection depends on fitness and prior
    therapy; separate trials do not establish superior tolerability to FOLFIRINOX.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24131140
    reference_title: Increased survival in pancreatic cancer with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine significantly improved overall survival,
      progression-free survival, and response rate, but rates of peripheral neuropathy
      and myelosuppression were increased.
    explanation: >-
      The Von Hoff et al. phase 3 trial demonstrated that nab-paclitaxel plus
      gemcitabine significantly improved overall survival (8.5 vs 6.7 months) in
      metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
- name: PARP Inhibitor Therapy
  description: >-
    Maintenance olaparib improves progression-free survival in metastatic PDAC with germline BRCA1/2
    pathogenic variants and no progression after at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum chemotherapy.
    POLO did not show a statistically significant overall-survival benefit in the final analysis.
    This evidence does not extend automatically to every DNA-repair alteration.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/jco.21.01604
    reference_title: 'Overall Survival Results From the POLO Trial: A Phase III Study of Active Maintenance Olaparib Versus Placebo for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The phase III POLO study demonstrated significant progression-free survival (PFS) benefit for active olaparib maintenance therapy versus placebo for patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and a germline BRCA mutation.
    explanation: The phase III POLO trial supports maintenance olaparib in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma; folded in from the former Metastatic_Pancreatic_Adenocarcinoma entry.
  - reference: PMID:31157963
    reference_title: Maintenance Olaparib for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial to
      evaluate the efficacy of olaparib as maintenance therapy in patients who had a
      germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer and disease
      that had not progressed during first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.
    explanation: >-
      The POLO trial demonstrated that maintenance olaparib significantly prolonged
      progression-free survival in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer
      patients who had not progressed on platinum-based chemotherapy.
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/jco.21.01604
    reference_title: 'Overall Survival Results From the POLO Trial: A Phase III Study of Active Maintenance Olaparib Versus Placebo for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: No statistically significant OS benefit was observed (median 19.0 v 19.2 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.83; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.22; P = .3487).
    explanation: >-
      Final POLO analysis qualifies the PFS benefit with the nonsignificant OS comparison.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: targeted therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
- name: Daraxonrasib (RAS(ON) Multiselective Inhibitor)
  description: >-
    Daraxonrasib is a cyclophilin-A-dependent inhibitor of active GTP-bound mutant and wild-type
    RAS. In phase III RASolute 302 for previously treated metastatic PDAC, median overall survival
    was 13.2 versus 6.6 months in the RAS G12 population (hazard ratio 0.40); median progression-free
    survival was 7.3 versus 3.5 months. These clinical outcomes establish treatment efficacy, not
    a universal resistance mechanism or an immune basis for survival benefit.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: daraxonrasib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:746946
        label: daraxonrasib
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: KRAS Oncogene Activation
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Daraxonrasib directly inhibits the active RAS(ON) state produced by
      oncogenic KRAS codon-12 mutations, the initiating driver of PDAC,
      suppressing constitutive RAS-MAPK signaling.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:42223072
      reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Daraxonrasib is an oral RAS(ON) multiselective, tri-complex inhibitor of
        the active guanosine triphosphate-bound state of mutant and wild-type RAS.
      explanation: >-
        The RASolute 302 report describes daraxonrasib's mechanism as direct
        inhibition of the active GTP-bound RAS state driven by mutant KRAS in PDAC.
  - target: Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition
    treatment_effect: ACTIVATES
    description: >-
      Preclinical PDAC immune remodeling follows RAS inhibition; this is not an inferred immune mechanism
      for the phase III survival effect.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40057911
      reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.
      explanation: >-
        Direct PDAC evidence was omitted from the immune report despite being cited in the resistance
        report.
  - target: Regulatory T-Cell Recruitment after KRAS Inhibition
    treatment_effect: ACTIVATES
    description: >-
      Treg recruitment is a model-dependent adaptation documented with daraxonrasib and MRTX1133.
    evidence:
    - reference: DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75960-3
      reference_title: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: Here, we demonstrate that Kras* targeting using MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib recruits diverse T-cell infiltrates, including regulatory (Tregs), effector and exhausted T cells into the PDAC microenvironment.
      explanation: >-
        Newer mouse PDAC evidence replaces the unsupported positive Treg-relief node.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT06625320
    reference_title: "RASolute 302: A Phase 3 Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized Study of Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) Versus Investigator's Choice of Standard of Care Therapy in Patients With Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel RAS(ON) inhibitor compared to standard(s) of care (SOC) treatment.
    explanation: ClinicalTrials.gov documents RASolute 302 as a phase 3 evaluation of the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib versus standard-of-care chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic PDAC.
  - reference: PMID:42223072
    reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Daraxonrasib is an oral RAS(ON) multiselective, tri-complex inhibitor of the active guanosine triphosphate-bound state of mutant and wild-type RAS.
    explanation: Establishes daraxonrasib's mechanism of action as a RAS(ON) multiselective tri-complex inhibitor of the active GTP-bound state of mutant and wild-type RAS, the basis for its target_mechanisms link to KRAS-centered signaling.
  - reference: PMID:42223072
    reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The median overall survival in the RAS G12 population was 13.2 months with daraxonrasib and 6.6 months with chemotherapy, and the median overall survival in the overall population was 13.2 months and 6.7 months, respectively; the hazard ratio was 0.40 in both populations (P<0.001).
    explanation: RASolute 302 demonstrated a significant overall survival benefit for daraxonrasib over chemotherapy (hazard ratio for death 0.40) in previously treated metastatic PDAC.
  notes: >-
    US regulatory status verified 4 September 2026: FDA approved daraxonrasib (Rasonque) on 26 August
    2026 for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior
    systemic therapy or are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. This indication is separate
    from the unvalidated checkpoint combinations. Source: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-daraxonrasib-metastatic-pancreatic-adenocarcinoma
- name: Experimental Mutant KRAS Vaccine for Residual Disease
  description: >-
    The phase I AMPLIFY-201 trial evaluated ELI-002 2P, an amphiphile G12D/G12R KRAS peptide vaccine
    plus CpG adjuvant, in patients with molecular residual KRAS-mutated pancreatic or colorectal
    cancer. It induced KRAS-specific T-cell responses. This early mixed-cancer study does not establish
    prevention in healthy high-risk individuals or randomized recurrence/survival benefit.
  therapeutic_modality: VACCINE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: vaccination
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15346
      label: Vaccination
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38195752
    reference_title: 'Lymph-node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic and colorectal cancer: the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Cancer vaccine ELI-002 2P enhances lymph node delivery and immune response using amphiphile (Amph) modification of G12D and G12R mutant KRAS (mKRAS) peptides (Amph-Peptides-2P) together with CpG oligonucleotide adjuvant (Amph-CpG-7909).
    explanation: >-
      Describes the mutant-KRAS amphiphile vaccine platform evaluated in the phase 1
      AMPLIFY-201 trial.
- name: Experimental KRAS Inhibition with Immune Checkpoint Blockade
  description: >-
    Checkpoint combinations with RAS inhibitors are supported by mouse PDAC experiments. RMC-7977/daraxonrasib
    plus PD-1-based therapy worked in one study, whereas a later study found CTLA-4 blockade specifically
    effective and associated with Treg reprogramming and tertiary lymphoid structures. Regimen, model,
    timing and checkpoint partner matter. These results do not establish routine clinical daraxonrasib-checkpoint
    treatment.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Immunotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15262
      label: Immunotherapy
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition
    treatment_effect: ACTIVATES
    description: >-
      Experimental combinations deepen immune-dependent tumor control.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40057911
      reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: the combination of RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitors with immunotherapy conferred deeper and more durable tumor regressions, including complete responses not seen with either treatment alone.
      explanation: >-
        Direct immunocompetent PDAC combination evidence.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75960-3
    reference_title: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: Kras* inhibition induces T-cell influx and offers a therapeutic window to specifically prime PDAC to anti-CTLA4 immune checkpoint blockade efficacy, in contrast to anti-PD1, anti-Tim3, anti-Lag3, anti-Vista, and anti-4-1BB agonist combination therapy.
    explanation: >-
      The newer model-specific comparison qualifies general checkpoint synergy.
- name: NALIRIFOX
  description: >-
    Liposomal irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil and leucovorin is a first-line option for fit
    patients with metastatic PDAC. NAPOLI 3 improved median overall survival to 11.1 versus 9.2 months
    compared with gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel; high-grade toxicity was frequent in both groups.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: liposomal irinotecan
      term:
        id: NCIT:C82676
        label: Irinotecan Sucrosofate
      description: >-
        The NCIT formulation term describes irinotecan encapsulated in liposomes; this is the
        liposomal irinotecan component of NALIRIFOX.
    - preferred_term: 5-fluorouracil
      term:
        id: CHEBI:46345
        label: 5-fluorouracil
    - preferred_term: leucovorin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:748997
        label: leucovorin
    - preferred_term: oxaliplatin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:31941
        label: oxaliplatin
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37708904
    reference_title: 'NALIRIFOX versus nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine in treatment-naive patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (NAPOLI 3): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Median overall survival was 11·1 months (95% CI 10·0-12·1) with NALIRIFOX versus 9·2 months (8·3-10·6) with nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine
    explanation: >-
      Randomized phase III evidence supports this contemporary chemotherapy option.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
- name: Zenocutuzumab for NRG1 Fusion-Positive Disease
  description: >-
    The HER2/HER3 bispecific antibody targets the NRG1-fusion signaling subset. In the phase II eNRGy
    trial, 15 of 36 evaluable pancreatic-cancer patients responded (42%); this single-arm molecularly
    selected result does not describe unselected PDAC.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Targeted Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: zenocutuzumab
      term:
        id: CHEBI:757449
        label: zenocutuzumab
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39908431
    reference_title: Efficacy of Zenocutuzumab in NRG1 Fusion-Positive Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 15 of 36 patients (42%; 95% CI, 25 to 59) with pancreatic cancer
    explanation: >-
      Pancreatic-cancer subgroup response in the NRG1-fusion-selected eNRGy trial.
  therapeutic_modality: MONOCLONAL_ANTIBODY
- name: Checkpoint Inhibition for MSI-High or Mismatch-Repair-Deficient Disease
  description: >-
    Mismatch-repair deficiency or high microsatellite instability identifies a small
    immune-treatment-sensitive subset. Responses in selected case series should not be generalized
    to microsatellite-stable PDAC or used as a population-wide response estimate. Pembrolizumab
    was used in eight of the nine immunotherapy-treated patients in the cited series; one received
    ipilimumab plus nivolumab, so the pooled response rate is not a pembrolizumab-only estimate.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Immunotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15262
      label: Immunotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: pembrolizumab
      term:
        id: NCIT:C106432
        label: Pembrolizumab
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1136/jitc-2021-004485
    reference_title: Detection of microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) by liquid biopsy predicts robust and durable response to immunotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The overall response rate by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors was 77% (7/9).
    explanation: >-
      A retrospective nine-patient MSI-high advanced pancreatic-cancer series supports subset activity;
      the small selected denominator limits precision.
  - reference: DOI:10.1136/jitc-2021-004485
    reference_title: Detection of microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) by liquid biopsy predicts robust and durable response to immunotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Eight out of nine patients received single-agent pembrolizumab (8/9), while one received
      ipilimumab plus nivolumab.
    explanation: >-
      The agent binding identifies the predominant treatment in this small retrospective series; the
      nine-patient outcome includes one different checkpoint regimen.
  therapeutic_modality: MONOCLONAL_ANTIBODY
- name: Nutritional Support
  description: >-
    Assess weight loss and dietary intake and provide individualized nutritional counseling and
    oral supplementation. Nutritional support complements treatment of exocrine insufficiency; it
    is not itself pancreatic enzyme replacement.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Supportive Care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32631175
    reference_title: "Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Improving the nutritional status, either with parenteral nutrition or oral supplementation,
      can increase the body weight, skeletal muscle mass, fat mass and quality of life, facilitating
      the administration of chemotherapy without interruption.
    explanation: >-
      The review background supports nutritional supplementation as supportive care. This entry
      concerns dietary counseling and oral support; parenteral nutrition is a separate medical route
      and is not represented by the BEHAVIORAL modality.
  therapeutic_modality: BEHAVIORAL
- name: Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement
  description: >-
    Pancreatic enzyme replacement, including pancrelipase, is used for exocrine insufficiency and
    maldigestion when indicated. Mixed observational/trial pooled survival associations do not
    establish a causal survival benefit; an 88-patient randomized trial of pancrelipase in
    unresectable pancreatic cancer did not improve the primary eight-week BMI endpoint.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Supportive Care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: pancrelipase
      term:
        id: CHEBI:753090
        label: pancrelipase
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32631175
    reference_title: 'Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)'
    explanation: >-
      Meta-analysis supports substantial exocrine insufficiency specifically in advanced pancreatic
      cancer; heterogeneity and tumor location limit generalization to all PDAC.
  - reference: PMID:29851751
    reference_title: A Multicenter Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Patients with unresectable PC receiving chemotherapy were randomly assigned to pancrelipase
      and nonpancrelipase groups.
    explanation: >-
      The randomized trial establishes the specific enzyme preparation used in this
      pancreatic-cancer population.
  - reference: PMID:29851751
    reference_title: A Multicenter Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In this randomized controlled trial, pancrelipase failed to improve the change in BMI at 8
      weeks in PC patients receiving chemotherapy.
    explanation: >-
      The null primary endpoint prevents presenting enzyme replacement as a proven general
      weight-gain or survival treatment; clinical use for exocrine insufficiency is a separate
      indication.
  therapeutic_modality: PROTEIN_REPLACEMENT
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
    description: >-
      Oral enzyme replacement supplies digestive enzymes to compensate for inadequate endogenous
      pancreatic enzyme delivery; it does not restore destroyed pancreatic tissue.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32631175
      reference_title: "Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: >-
        Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) is the standard treatment for PEI.
      explanation: >-
        The review describes symptomatic enzyme replacement for exocrine insufficiency, independently
        of uncertain survival benefit.
- name: Biliary Drainage
  description: >-
    Endoscopic placement of a fully covered self-expandable metallic biliary stent can relieve
    malignant biliary obstruction. Select procedural drainage according to anatomy, symptoms and
    the clinical treatment plan.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Supportive Care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41067164
    reference_title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: In the event of biliary obstruction, endoscopic placement of a fully covered, self-expandable metallic biliary stent is suggested
    explanation: >-
      Guideline addresses biliary obstruction.
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Obstructive Jaundice
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
    description: >-
      Biliary stenting bypasses the obstructed segment and restores drainage in patients with
      malignant biliary obstruction.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41067164
      reference_title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with pancreatic cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: In the event of biliary obstruction, endoscopic placement of a fully covered, self-expandable metallic biliary stent is suggested
      explanation: >-
        Guideline addresses biliary obstruction.
- name: Pain Management
  description: >-
    Provide individualized pain assessment and specialist-guided multimodal analgesia alongside
    cancer-directed therapy. This supportive-care category spans medication and procedural
    approaches, so it does not designate one pharmacologic platform or a single therapeutic agent.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Supportive Care
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15747
      label: Supportive Care
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41067164
    reference_title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with pancreatic cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Effective pain control is strongly recommended and should involve a pain control specialist when required
    explanation: >-
      Guideline supports active specialist pain management.
  therapeutic_modality: OTHER
- name: Experimental RAS-EGFR-STAT3 Combination
  description: >-
    Daraxonrasib, afatinib and the STAT3 degrader SD36 produced prolonged regressions in orthotopic,
    genetically engineered and patient-derived xenograft PDAC models. This corrected primary study
    also tested genetic RAF1/EGFR/STAT3 ablation. It supports combination research, not routine patient
    treatment or proof that immunity is irrelevant.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Targeted Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: daraxonrasib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:746946
        label: daraxonrasib
    - preferred_term: afatinib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:61390
        label: afatinib
    - preferred_term: SD36
      term:
        id: NCIT:C200712
        label: STAT3 Inhibitor
      description: >-
        SD36 is the experimental STAT3-targeting degrader used in the cited study. The binding is to
        the broader STAT3 inhibitor class: OLS searches of CHEBI and NCIT found no specific SD36 or
        SD-36 entity on 5 September 2026.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: KRAS Oncogene Activation
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Daraxonrasib inhibits active RAS within the experimental daraxonrasib-afatinib-SD36
      combination. Linking the same treatment to RAS signaling and observed resistance prevention
      connects the experimental resistance branch without asserting that initiating KRAS activation
      causes acquired amplification in untreated tumors.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:42224594
      reference_title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: a combination of selective inhibitors of KRAS (RMC-6236/daraxonrasib), EGFR family (afatinib), and STAT3 (SD36) induced the complete regression of orthotopic PDAC tumors with no evidence of tumor resistance for over 200 d posttreatment.
      explanation: >-
        The corrected mouse-model study identifies daraxonrasib as the KRAS/RAS-directed component of
        the combination. This pharmacologic target link does not establish acquired amplification as a
        consequence of the initiating mutation or identify a human resistance frequency.
  - target: Acquired RAS(ON) Inhibitor Resistance
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Experimental multilevel pathway inhibition delayed or prevented detected resistance within
      the studied follow-up.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:42224594
      reference_title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: a combination of selective inhibitors of KRAS (RMC-6236/daraxonrasib), EGFR family (afatinib), and STAT3 (SD36) induced the complete regression of orthotopic PDAC tumors with no evidence of tumor resistance for over 200 d posttreatment.
      explanation: >-
        Corrected republication supports pharmacologic mouse-model durability; no human efficacy
        or permanent cure is established.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42224594
    reference_title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: a combination of selective inhibitors of KRAS (RMC-6236/daraxonrasib), EGFR family (afatinib), and STAT3 (SD36) induced the complete regression of orthotopic PDAC tumors with no evidence of tumor resistance for over 200 d posttreatment.
    explanation: >-
      Corrected republication supports pharmacologic mouse-model durability; no human efficacy or
      permanent cure is established.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
clinical_trials:
- name: NCT06625320
  description: >-
    RASolute 302: a phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial comparing
    daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) with the investigator's choice of standard chemotherapy
    in patients with previously treated metastatic PDAC. The trial met its dual
    primary endpoints of overall survival and progression-free survival in the
    RAS G12 population.
  phase: PHASE_III
  target_phenotypes:
  - preferred_term: Neoplasm of the pancreas
    term:
      id: HP:0002894
      label: Neoplasm of the pancreas
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT06625320
    reference_title: "RASolute 302: A Phase 3 Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized Study of Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) Versus Investigator's Choice of Standard of Care Therapy in Patients With Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel
      RAS(ON) inhibitor compared to standard(s) of care (SOC) treatment.
    explanation: >-
      ClinicalTrials.gov confirms RASolute 302 (NCT06625320) evaluated the RAS(ON)
      inhibitor daraxonrasib against standard-of-care chemotherapy in mPDAC.
  - reference: PMID:42223072
    reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Among patients with previously treated mPDAC, treatment with daraxonrasib led
      to significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than
      chemotherapy.
    explanation: >-
      The primary-results publication reports that RASolute 302 met its overall
      survival and progression-free survival endpoints favoring daraxonrasib.
- name: NCT04083235
  description: >-
    NAPOLI 3 randomized first-line NALIRIFOX against gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel in metastatic pancreatic
    ductal adenocarcinoma.
  phase: PHASE_III
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37708904
    reference_title: 'NALIRIFOX versus nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine in treatment-naive patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (NAPOLI 3): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Median overall survival was 11·1 months (95% CI 10·0-12·1) with NALIRIFOX versus 9·2 months (8·3-10·6) with nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine
    explanation: >-
      Published randomized trial provides the outcome; no live recruitment-status claim is inferred.
- name: NCT02184195
  description: >-
    POLO randomized maintenance olaparib versus placebo in germline BRCA1/2 metastatic pancreatic
    cancer without progression on first-line platinum; PFS improved but final OS was not statistically
    different.
  phase: PHASE_III
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/jco.21.01604
    reference_title: 'Overall Survival Results From the POLO Trial: A Phase III Study of Active Maintenance Olaparib Versus Placebo for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The phase III POLO study demonstrated significant progression-free survival (PFS) benefit for active olaparib maintenance therapy versus placebo for patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and a germline BRCA mutation.
    explanation: The phase III POLO trial supports maintenance olaparib in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma; folded in from the former Metastatic_Pancreatic_Adenocarcinoma entry.
  - reference: PMID:31157963
    reference_title: Maintenance Olaparib for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial to
      evaluate the efficacy of olaparib as maintenance therapy in patients who had a
      germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer and disease
      that had not progressed during first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.
    explanation: >-
      The POLO trial demonstrated that maintenance olaparib significantly prolonged
      progression-free survival in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer
      patients who had not progressed on platinum-based chemotherapy.
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/jco.21.01604
    reference_title: 'Overall Survival Results From the POLO Trial: A Phase III Study of Active Maintenance Olaparib Versus Placebo for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: No statistically significant OS benefit was observed (median 19.0 v 19.2 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.83; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.22; P = .3487).
    explanation: >-
      Final POLO analysis qualifies the PFS benefit with the nonsignificant OS comparison.
- name: NCT02715804
  description: >-
    HALO 109-301 compared PEGPH20 plus gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel with placebo plus chemotherapy
    in hyaluronan-high metastatic PDAC. Increased response rate did not improve survival, limiting
    clinical translation of stromal hyaluronan depletion.
  phase: PHASE_III
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32706635
    reference_title: Randomized Phase III Trial of Pegvorhyaluronidase Alfa With Nab-Paclitaxel Plus Gemcitabine for Patients With Hyaluronan-High Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: The addition of PEGPH20 to AG increased the ORR but did not improve OS or PFS.
    explanation: >-
      Randomized trial limits extrapolation from preclinical matrix/hypoperfusion rescue to clinical
      survival.
discussions:
- discussion_id: gap_pdac_caf_program_t_cell_exclusion
  prompt: >-
    Which cancer-associated fibroblast programs actively cause T-cell exclusion
    and checkpoint resistance in PDAC, and which stromal programs are
    tumor-restraining or merely correlative with desmoplastic burden?
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  attaches_to:
  - pathophysiology#Desmoplastic Stroma
  - pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
  - pathophysiology#Immune Evasion
  rationale: >-
    PDAC desmoplasia is not a single therapeutic target: some CAF states may
    exclude effector T cells, whereas others may restrain invasion. A
    patient-derived organ-on-chip experiment can test whether specific CAF
    programs are causal for immune exclusion and whether reprogramming them
    improves T-cell cytotoxicity without removing tumor-restraining stroma.
  proposed_experiments:
  - experiment_id: exp_pdac_patient_ooc_caf_t_cell_exclusion
    name: Patient-derived PDAC organ-on-chip CAF reprogramming and T-cell infiltration assay
    description: >-
      Assemble a patient-derived PDAC organoid organ-on-chip with fibroblasts,
      endothelium, and immune cells; induce or suppress CAF programs including
      interferon-response CAF states; then measure T-cell infiltration,
      cytotoxicity, tumor viability, and stromal remodeling under checkpoint
      blockade.
    experiment_type:
      preferred_term: patient-derived organ-on-chip immunotherapy perturbation experiment
    model_systems:
    - name: Patient-derived PDAC tumor-microenvironment organ-on-chip
      description: >-
        Microfluidic human PDAC model combining patient-derived tumor organoids
        with fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune cells so stromal
        crosstalk, T-cell migration, and drug response can be measured in a
        standardized ex vivo platform.
      experimental_model_type: ORGAN_ON_CHIP
      namo_type: namo:OrganOnChip
      organism:
        preferred_term: human
        term:
          id: NCBITaxon:9606
          label: Homo sapiens
      tissue_term:
        preferred_term: pancreas
        term:
          id: UBERON:0001264
          label: pancreas
      cell_types:
      - preferred_term: pancreatic ductal cell
        term:
          id: CL:0002079
          label: pancreatic ductal cell
      - preferred_term: fibroblast
        term:
          id: CL:0000057
          label: fibroblast
      - preferred_term: endothelial cell
        term:
          id: CL:0000115
          label: endothelial cell
      - preferred_term: T cell
        term:
          id: CL:0000084
          label: T cell
      cell_source: patient-derived organoids plus matched stromal and immune-cell compartments
      culture_system: perfused microfluidic organ-on-chip with extracellular-matrix scaffold
    perturbations:
    - name: CAF subtype induction and depletion
      target: pathophysiology#Desmoplastic Stroma
      description: >-
        Induce, suppress, or selectively deplete CAF states to separate
        immune-excluding and tumor-restraining stromal programs.
      genes:
      - preferred_term: FAP
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: extracellular matrix organization
        term:
          id: GO:0030198
          label: extracellular matrix organization
    - name: STING-driven interferon-response CAF induction
      target: pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
      description: >-
        STING agonism or matched interferon-response induction used to test
        whether an interferon-response CAF state decreases invasion and improves
        antitumor immune activity.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: type I interferon signaling pathway
        term:
          id: GO:0060337
          label: type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway
    - name: Immune checkpoint blockade
      target: pathophysiology#Immune Evasion
      description: >-
        Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or matched checkpoint blockade applied with CAF
        perturbation to test whether stromal reprogramming is required for
        T-cell cytotoxicity.
      treatment_term:
        preferred_term: immunotherapy
        term:
          id: NCIT:C15262
          label: Immunotherapy
    readouts:
    - name: T-cell infiltration and cytotoxicity
      target: pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
      description: >-
        Spatial T-cell entry into tumor organoid regions, activation markers,
        and tumor-cell killing after CAF-state perturbation.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: T cell activation
        term:
          id: GO:0042110
          label: T cell activation
      assays:
      - preferred_term: high-content live imaging
      - preferred_term: cytotoxicity assay
      direction: NEGATIVE
    - name: CAF-state trajectory
      target: pathophysiology#Desmoplastic Stroma
      description: >-
        Single-cell and spatial profiling of inflammatory, myofibroblastic, and
        interferon-response CAF programs after stromal perturbation.
      assays:
      - preferred_term: single-cell transcriptomic profiling
      - preferred_term: spatial transcriptomic profiling
      direction: POSITIVE
    - name: Tumor organoid viability under checkpoint blockade
      target: pathophysiology#Immune Evasion
      description: Tumor-cell survival after combined CAF perturbation and checkpoint blockade.
      assays:
      - preferred_term: cell viability assay
      direction: NEGATIVE
    controls:
    - name: Tumor organoid without CAF compartment
      description: Patient-derived PDAC organoid chip lacking fibroblasts.
    - name: CAF-intact chip without T cells
      description: Stromal chip lacking effector T cells to distinguish direct stromal effects from immune-mediated killing.
    - name: Isotype-control checkpoint antibody
      description: Matched antibody control for checkpoint blockade.
    decision_criterion: >-
      A causal CAF immune-exclusion program is supported if its induction
      reduces T-cell entry or killing and its suppression restores checkpoint
      response. A tumor-restraining CAF state is supported if induction lowers
      invasion or viability while preserving or improving T-cell function.
    would_support:
    - pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
    - pathophysiology#Immune Evasion
    would_refute:
    - pathophysiology#CAF-Mediated T Cell Exclusion
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41610338
      reference_title: A Patient-Derived Organ-on-Chip Platform for Modeling the Tumor Microenvironment and Drug Responses in Pancreatic Cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: incorporating PDOs with key components of the TME (fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune cells) within a microfluidic system
      explanation: >-
        Provides the recent patient-derived organ-on-chip precedent for a
        PDAC tumor-microenvironment experiment with stromal and immune
        compartments.
    - reference: PMID:41610338
      reference_title: A Patient-Derived Organ-on-Chip Platform for Modeling the Tumor Microenvironment and Drug Responses in Pancreatic Cancer.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: model and assess the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade for T cell cytotoxicity in PDAC
      explanation: >-
        Supports using this platform to adjudicate checkpoint response in the
        presence of patient-derived stromal context.
    - reference: PMID:40215177
      reference_title: Dissecting FAP+ Cell Diversity in Pancreatic Cancer Uncovers an Interferon-Response Subtype of Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts with Tumor-Restraining Properties.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: identifies an ifCAF subtype that can be induced to suppress protumorigenic features of PDAC
      explanation: >-
        Motivates testing CAF reprogramming rather than treating all desmoplasia
        as uniformly protumorigenic.
